And when I was hitting the right keys this keyboard did keep up with me, so that is another point in its favor. Bottom line: if you are accustomed to full size keyboards and have BIG hands this may, in fact, be the keyboard for you. It's mechanically sound, but if I am any indication, it's not for everyone.

title: Rickenbacker is PAINFUL to your strumming arm!
text: I'm a huge Beatles, Lennon, and Rickenbacker fan. But this guitar is flat-out uncomfortable and painful to use in Rock Band. I'm talking about your strumming arm - the part of your forearm that contacts the edge of the guitar is just beat-up to no end while you're playing. There's no comfortable place to put your arm anywhere on the guitar while strumming. In stark contrast, the standard Rock Band Fender guitars always have a nice angled area that is perfectly designed for this issue. I'm not pleased, and am planning on returning the guitar. For this much money, it has to feel good as well as play good. (And I will add that playing is perfect - spot on. No glitches or issues with the keys, the wireless reception, nothing. It's great) One other note - I've heard from many other people online and in person that both the McCartney Bass and the Harrison Gretch have the same issue - painful strumming forearm syndrome (PSFS) "Puss-Fuss" is no laughing matter.

title: Singstar pales in comparison to Karaoke Revolution - just not fun
text: My wife and I have tried all of the karaoke games available for PS2 - and Singstar is the worst. It's not even close. First, the inability to dial down the voice but leave the background music is enough alone to dump this for a good used Karaoke Revolution. Then the mics - they're MUCH heavier - perhaps 5-10x as heavy as the K-R microphones, and much bigger meaning harder to store when you put everything away. The game itself, well it's not really a game. It's just karaoke. K-R is a game, where you compete, unlock things, win trophies, etc. SS does allow you unlock a few songs, but the gameplay is boring and unfulfilling. The scoring is obnoxious and annoying compared to K-R as well. It grades 10x more for singing the exact PHRASING as the original than singing on pitch. Go buy a PS2 - they're terrific. Then go to ebay and type in KARAOKE REVOLUTION PS2 and actually enjoy singing into your TV.

title: Great upgrade to the old rules
text: I had copies of the original version of Necromunda. It was a great game that required solid tactical planning. The different gangs each had a unique quirk that allowed for quite a bit of individuality in play and planning. This is a nice upgrade, adding more streamlined rules and simplifying the character stats. If you are intrigued by the Warhammer 40K universe this is a way to get introduced, but understand that this is not the same rule set. Its similar but this game uses an individual movement system rather than the squad based movement and fighting of the larger game. I really enjoy this game, it allows a lot of individuality. It does have some issues with balance in long campaigns as luck with gang members surviving fights can contribute into some gangs being far more powerful than others, but its always a challenging puzzle.

title: Winning the world with trade
text: I quickly found that republics end up with lots of money, especially if properly managed. Of course, they also have the potential to spend even greater amounts of money. I think this is my favorite of the expansions. It offers a new twist to the game, and definitely requires a different touch. Republics rely much more on mercenaries and trade, which is a definite change. Even their marriages adjust as you now can end up paying money to arrange an advantageous marriage to the neighboring duke. (if you can convince him to wed his daughter to a common merchant.) Not much else new, but anyone picking up this DLC probably already has the original game and has discovered the time-consuming fun and frustration that is Crusader Kings.

title: Hold off the Zerg Rush
text: I like this expansion and yet also hate this expansion. Overall, the new mechanics are well balanced. You can now play pagans, and work with the limitations of the religion. for the Norse, this means you can't avoid having each of your children inheriting and having to go to war or raiding every year or 2. It makes for a lot of early conflict. The game does try to help at first, as the initial Norse counties have high levels of troops and a few pre-planned invasions. This makes it easy to get some quick conquests in. Of course, that has a flip side. If you are facing this onslaught (Scotland, England, Ireland, Holland, etc.) you end up facing 20-30 years of heavy conflict, and will likely lose quite a few provinces early. And if you want to play as an independent count in any Norse region or one they are likely to attack expect to end up conquered because they will hit hard at first. But once their initial leaders start dying the kingdoms tend to come apart with internal conflicts. So they really only have a major effect on the game for the first 50 years and then it does down a bit despite their need to keep raiding. (by then its hard to raid from a single province and the fragmentation of their kingdoms means they don't have multiple provinces to use.) Good, but it basically just sets up a huge Zerg-rush at the start and then it settles down to the old game.

title: Nice graphics, but the original was more fun
text: I don't know why, but the original was a lot more fun than this was. The graphics here are much nicer and you can actually ride the coasters and waterslides you make, but something was missing. I think its the same thing that has been ruining most tycoon style games for me. I play these games mostly for the tycoon aspects. I like having decent graphics, but for me the key is always the struggle to get some money and the question of if I can make the business work. RCT 3 minimized that aspect to push the graphics and a few other features that were unsatisfying for me. This is not a bad game, but it doesn't do anything special and the original has more coaster types and options. The only advantage RCT3 has is the graphics and the fact that its new enough to work with less trouble on the latest version of Windows.

title: My niece and nephew loved this
text: My family isn't much into games with the exception of rummy and other card games. This means that I usually struggle to get any member of my family to try any of the games I bring with me when we are going to get together. However, when I described this one my sister was willing to allow her children (8 and 6) to try it. There was a bit of a problem getting my 6 year old niece to understand how things go, and neither of the children did a good job of looking and planning ahead, but both loved the game and immediately wanted to play again. The game itself is so simple its almost scary. Setup takes only a few minutes and game play is straightforward, with no dice or cards involved. I managed to teach a 6 year old how to play and while the strategy might confuse her, she still had a wonderful time. This is a great gateway game or one for a quiet afternoon when no one wants to have to think while playing a game. I definitely recommend this one.

title: Adds more nations, but not a huge game changer
text: The more I play Crusader Kings, the more I find myself thinking that the programmers think themselves entirely too clever. This DLC definitely helped dramatize that for me. The truth was that I found that this didn't add as much as I expected. With this expansion you can now play nations that start with an "Islamic" government. These nations operate under slightly different rules (such as receiving a prestige penalty for not having multiple wives.) But after you get around the few new quirks, the game is much the same. Through a combination of alliances, military actions and patience you are attempting to take your ruler's dynasty and make them rulers over as much of hte world as possible. I found this fun, but only for a while. In the end this DLC was not a huge boost to the playability of hte game, so I'm sticking with 3 stars. Overall the game is fun, but in solo play it doesn't really keep ones attention for very long. (I cannot speak on the multi-player aspects because I avoid online play.)

title: Playable and time consuming, but not special
text: This is a game that can definitely burn a number of hours as you build up forces and try to conquer the world. In style of play it most resembles Elemental or Civ V than other older turn-based 4X games. I have to say that I liked elemenats of hte game, but could not call this a masterpiece. The standard for most fantasy 4X games is still Master of Magic. Yes, the graphics are terrible, but the shear number of races and spells and the addition of heroes made the game a huge step up compared to the other options. Age of Wonders tries to capture the same elements, but for me it never quite achieved the same elegance. Warlock doesn't try to be as expansive as Master of Magic. There are only 3 races and no technology tree. The only research is for spells, and the research tree is rather linear, you see 5 options to research and from what I could see the system works by a "researched X spell and spell X+1 appears in the tree. The spells appear to follow a very linear tech tree. Combat is not much different than Civ V, the lack of stacking makes it a bit more tactically than Civ IV, but it's still rather straightforward in execution. Honestly, this feels like it could have been a lot better if more time had been spent expanding options. The lack of races, the lack of a tech tree, the linear nature of spell research, all leaft me thinking the game could be so much more. But I love 4X games, so I still enjoy this one. It plays faster and smoother than Elemental, and while lacking in some elements, does not have the same balance issues that make Elemental nearly impossible to enjoy. If you like 4X games, and like the idea of adding magic, this is worth trying. Otherwise, it will likely frustrate you.

title: Fun,simple, not much more
text: I have enjoyed playing this game since I purchased it. It's simple to play, and entertaining. However, it isn't a deep game, nor does it really present challenges which offer a feelign of reward when they are completed. Despite the quest system laid over the Sims engine, this game has a limited range of options. I am not even sure I'd say this is a "simulation" game, even through it claims to be the Sims. You decide what path your sim will follow when you create them. To play you ahve to select a quest from a list of 6 that will be avaiable, dependent on what buildings and sims you have available. Completion of quests improves your kingdom and gives you money that can be used to purchase food and furniture for your sim. The quests are rather straightforward and usually have a combination of 4 basic steps. 1) go to a location 2) obtain certain items 3) talk to certain sims 4) interact with an event point or person (may include fighting) Finishing a quest with a high score requires concentrating on the steps while keeping your sim fed, and entertained. Depending on the "fatal flaw" you have your sims that could be harder. Some flaws have a greater effect than others. As I said, i have had fun playing hte game and exploring the world, but it is limited. This game is not one that truly offers an infinite amount of gameplay. Eventually even with new quests there just won't be anything that feels "new" available to perform. The achievements are interesting, but most just require that you play a certain amount ot time to achieve. A few require planning, but are otherwise achievable. I'd say this game is good for lovers of Sims2 and Sims3, not bad for those who like RPGs and want to try one that's a bit more talk than fight, but will definitely bore those who enjoy the energy rush of first-person shooters and sports games.

title: Great fun!
text: It's hard to imagine that a game about being a pirate could be fun, but this game breaks all the rules about what is fun. Who knew that a game of sailing from city to city could turn into an adventure. But that is what makes Pirates! special. This is not a simple trading game. Sure you can make money being a peaceful trader and sailing between ports, but the game truly comes into its own when you get into the spirit of the game and attack one faction or another. Once you join in the fighting, you can attack cities or ships, woo the daughters of governors allied to your nation, defeat pirates and find the treasure they buried on land, and search for your kidnapped family. The controls can take a little time to get used to and swordfights are definitely a challenge at first, but the game easily becomes one where you start playing saying "I'll play for 1 hour" and when you finally look back at the clock 5 or more hours have passed as you terrorized the Spanish Armada and raided the treasure fleet. This is a great game for all ages.

title: Civilization in Space
text: More than any other 4X game this one comes closest to being Civilization in space. As others have noted the interface is very busy, and the game does sometimes bog you down with details such as custom designing a ship, or deciding what upgrade to build next as your colony worlds. It's a good game, and fun if you enjoy 4x turn-based strategy. I can't give the game 5 stars though. The AI is not well programmed and the computer races will regularly take actions that display the limitations of the programming. Worse, there are times that no computer race will sign a treaty with you, even though you have been perfectly honorable up to that point. I have played several games where at some point I'm ready to pull my hair out because of the illogic the computer uses. It even extends to surrendering. You could have the last 1-2 worlds of one computer race surrounded and he'll suddenly surrender to a third race rather than allow you to defeat him. This is extremely frustrating, especially if you are trying to get a conquest win as you then have to start a new war with an enemy who might have been a friend up to that point. Still, its fun, has an amazing amount of detail and technologies to research, and does not have a vertical learning curve. If you like 4X games, its worth looking into, but those who don't have the patience for the slow pace of most turn-based games should avoid this.

title: Send in the Zerg Rush!
text: This is one where I have to admit that the description of the game fooled me completely. I try to avoid RTS games because they always seem to devolve into click fests where the goal is not to use superior planning or tactics, but simply to overwhelm any opponent with numbers and fierocity. Seven Kingdoms 2 proved to be a poor mans Age of Mythology. There isn't as much variation in the troop types and if you play one of the 7 monster races you don't really have any buildings to create other than the occasional additional lair to help entice other monsters to fight for you. I was particularly disappointed after playing the short tutorial as it pretty much tells you to use the "zerg rush" approach to conquer the final city. For RTS lovers this might prove to be an afternoon's diversion as the monster races do add a new twist to an old standard, but for anyone else this will be a very boring clickfest and unlikely to remain on their comptuer long.

title: Not real football, but definitely real fun!
text: I had known about the board game long before this game came out for the PC. I even had the old DOS based version of this game that came out some 15 year ago. That did not prepare me for the sheer fun of this game. The original story had some dwarves and orcs stumbling on a stadium and finding some old footballers equipment. Thanks to a wise dwarf who managed to decipher an old "Nuffle" NFL) rule book and who declared that this stadium was used for some kind of religious ceremony for the high priest Roz-el. The orcs and dwarves decided to try a football game, only with some very modified rules. The game itself plays more like rugby than football with a fast paced feel as both teams bash each other attempting to carry the ball into the end zone. The original rules are turn based, and the programmers have one version that holds true to those rules. For those wanting even more of a challenge, there is real-time play as well. The graphics are solid, and although the voiceovers do become very repetitive, they are quite amusing at first. A lot of well considered effort went into making this game fun and challenging. It definitely delivers on that promise.

title: Great fun!
text: I've always been a huge fan of console RPGs, but usually find that I cannot manage to finish any game. I'll play for a while, but eventually the experience gets dull and I stop. This game is one where after 60 hours played, I'm not only still playing, but actually looking for more to do, even if its just wandering the ocean on my golem looking for new islands to pick up. Others have talked about most of the aspects. The game itself is not completely unique, but it is rare. Crafting is simple, but a good deal of planning must go into obtaining the resources for many of the best items, and obtaining recipes usually means completing quests for the games NPCs. Getting those quests usually requires a high level of friendship with the NPC, so again, there's a lot of planning to put into the game. My only complaint would be the camera issue others have noted. You have limited control of the camera and there have been times I got stuck behind a wall until I could get the camera to rotate the view. Frustrating, but hardly a game breaker.

title: Better than Civ V, but no Master of Magic
text: I remember the original Civilization. it's spawned many copies and variants since then, one of those being Master of Magic, which kept the basic theme of Civ, but added in races and magic to the mix. It also gave us the first appearance of heros. Many of hte original writeups about Elemental suggested that it was going to be the sequel to Master of Magic. I looked forward to getting it, as I love this type of game, and trying to run the odl Dos Master of Magic on my computer doesn't work all that well. Sadly, when Elemental first came out it did have major bugs taht left the game nearly unplayable. Fortunately Stardock didn't quit on the game and they have made numerous refinements and improvements. I have no had a crash in months, and the game appears stable. Unfortunately, it still is no Master of Magic. The races are divided effectively into a light and dark side and the dark "Empire" races have a huge initial advantage due to their tech tree. They don't get some of hte top Techs that the light "Kingdom" races can obtain if they have enough time, but they do have a huge early advantage. It doesn't help taht the AI isn't very good especially at dealing with a well organized "stack of death". If you have time to put together a powerful stack of 8-9 high level units, you can easily crush anything the computer sends against you. Tactics tend to be simple. Keep one stack together and build it up to a high level doing quests and killing the wandering monsters until its powerful enough to kill anything it faces. The game is in my mind better than Civ V. It doesn't have the city states, but it offers more choices in the city management and tech choices. A good game, but not a great one. I hate that I paid full price considering what I know now, but its not a horrible deal either.

title: This is not Civilization
text: Like many of the other reviewers, I've played and enjoyed the Civilization series since the first one came out back when I was in college. Each one seemed to improve on the previous one, with new elements merging well with the established tactics and strategies. Sadly, this latest version removes elements that worked and added in new changes that pretty much ruined the game itself, at least as far as being Civilzation. If the makers had given it a different name, I would not have been as disappointed, but without the name, I also probably would not have purchased it. I have already removed Civ V from my computer and gone back to playing Civ IV. It doesn't have the same graphics, but 4X type games are not supposed to be graphics masterpieces, so I don't miss much there. I play for the experience and fun, something that Civ V left out when updating hte graphics and playing with the rules of population happiness.

title: Good addition to my work computer
text: This is such An amazing purchase! I have been using a wired mouse provided by my company for the past two years. This mouse was on a promotional sale, combined with my Amazon credit card cash back, I decided to give this one a try. It is AMAZING! It works so well with my work PC, and it somehow successfully installed the software in my work laptop without any issues. It is very convenient to carry for meetings, and a lot more sensitive and smooth than the cheap one I was using. The battery life is surprisingly long also. I have accidentally left the mouse turned on for a few nights, it still lasted the whole week for me! Anyway, great deal for great product, this is a good brand for gaming and non gaming purposes. Hope this helps.

title: A Game that is Tons of Fun!
text: Quite a while ago now I purchased this Wonderful game, ”Splatoon 2" for the Nintendo Switch.. and I have to say that I have really enjoyed it! Even though I had owned a Wii U for several years.. somehow I had simply never picked up the original "Splatoon" game for it. So when "Splatoon 2" came out for the Nintendo Switch, I knew I had to give it a try. I am very glad that I did! The gameplay is really amazing.. and it is loads of Fun! I can see why this title has been such a huge hit!

title: Very Nice (and Useful Product)!
text: A while ago I purchased this item, the Nintendo Switch Wired Internet LAN Adapter by HORI (Officially Licensed by Nintendo) .. and I must say that thus far I am very satisfied with it! I bought this Wired Internet LAN Adapter in the hopes that it would provide a more stable internet connection for my Nintendo Switch (while it is withinn the Dock).. in addition to the standard Wi-Fi connection that I typically use (whenever my Switch in not Docked). So far it seems to work just fine! In case you don't know, this process basically works pretty much as expected: As long as my Nintendo Switch is within the Dock (and thus connected to my TV) the Wired Internet LAN Adapter is used to connect it to the internet. But as soon as I remove my Switch from the Dock (using the Switch as a handheld device).. the active internet connection automatically switches over to my Wi-Fi connection. And of course whenever I place my Switch back into the Dock.. The Wired internet connection becomes active once again. The Wired Internet LAN Adapter was also very easy to connect to my Nintendo Switch console. The adapter simply plugs into the blue USB connector on the Dock. As I said I am very happy with it!

title: Very useful and well-made product!!
text: A short time after I purchased my Nintendo Switch console, I also bought this Excellent item, the HORI Compact Playstand for Nintendo Switch (Officially Licensed by Nintendo). I am very glad that I did! If you think you will probably be using your Nintendo Switch often in what is commonly referred to as "Table Top" mode, then you will most likely want to pick up one of these incredibly useful Play Stand accessories. The Play Stand itself is very easy to use, and it provides you with three different viewing angles. And, because this Play Stand raises your Nintendo Switch up off of the table, you can then connect a USB C type connector to the bottom of your Switch, thus allowing you to charge your system, while the play Stand is being used. This is a nice plus. The HORI Play Stand is well-constructed.. and I would definitely​ recommend it to anyone who owns a Nintendo Switch!

title: Really Fantastic Controller!!
text: A while ago now (back shortly after I had first bought my Nintendo Switch console) I had also purchased this Fantastic item, the Nintendo Switch Pro Controller (by Nintendo). And I have to say that I am most pleased with it! This controller is amazing! And it works very well. I highly recommend it to anyone who plans to purchase a Nintendo Switch. You won't be disappointed. Now.. don't get me wrong.. The standard joy-con controllers, which come with the Nintendo Switch work fine as well. They really do. But, if you are like me, I am sure you can appreciate the option for purchasing a more standard type of game controller.. And the Nintendo Switch Pro Controller is an excellent choice! It feels great in the hands, and is highly responsive.. exactly what you would expect from a well-built Nintendo brand controller. If you're thinking about getting a Nintendo Switch console, you really should consider also investing in this great controller! It will just give you a more classic way of playing your games. And you'll find that you will prefer playing certain titles with this controller. It is that good.

title: Really Excellent Nintendo Switch accessory!
text: A while ago now (way back when I first bought my Nintendo Switch console) I also purchased this fine item, the Nintendo Switch - Joy-Con Charging Grip (by Nintendo). I must say that I'm very happy with it. This item allows me to charge my Nintendo Switch Joy con controllers using an included USB charging cable, which I can easily plug in to the Nintendo Switch Dock. The item is really easy to use and I can even charge the controllers while I am using them to play games. This device really comes in handy if you buy extra joycon controllers.. because you can use it to charge them up.. while keeping the original two controllers attached to the switch itself to keep them charged. This is a very good product!

title: Really Great Product!!
text: I just recently purchased this fine item, the "amFilm Tempered Glass Screen Protector for Nintendo Switch 2017 (2-Pack)" and I must say that I am very pleased with it! Let me start off by saying that I am not really good at installing this type of item, in fact I have never done anything like this before. So I was glad that this screen protector package includes two tempered glass screens within each set.. I presume that this is just in case you are not totally happy with your first attempt at installing this product. That is sort of what happened to me. I installed the first tempered glass screen protector fairly easily.. except for the fact that I ended up with one small piece of dust that became trapped beneath the screen protector during installation. I must stress that this error was due solely to my own actions, and not because of any flaws in the product. It was due to my inexperience. I ultimately ended up removing by screen protector completely, which of course rendered the first tempered glass screen protector useless. And I started over fresh, using second tempered glass screen protector contained in the set. My second attempt at installing this item was successful.. and I am very pleased with the end result! I was able to find a video on YouTube detailing how to install a tempered glass screen protector on the Nintendo Switch.. using what was called the "Hinge Method". (The "Hinge Method" basically involves using some tape to secure the screen protector securely to the Nintendo Switch during installation.. and I recommend using this method.) This screen protector seems to be a really Wonderful and well made product! I am most pleased!

title: The promise of additional content for a tremendous game..
text: I recently purchased the "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild Expansion Pass" (for the Nintendo Switch game) ..and I'm hoping that it will prove to be a very good buy! Thus far, I am really loving the game "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild!" And this expansion pass promises to add even more new content to the game at some point later this year. Although most of the additional content is not available yet.. I'm betting that it will definitely be worth the price of the expansion pass ..based on what I've already seen within the game.

title: Fantastic game so far!
text: I recently purchased the Nintendo Switch version of the game "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" and I must say I am very pleased with it! Keep in mind I haven't played it for very long, ..but this game appears to be simply awesome! Breath of the Wild definitely looks like a game that I am going to be playing for a long, long time to come. The sheer size and depth of the world (and it's gameplay) seems incredible. As a huge fan of the Zelda series I was hoping this game would be something special.. and that most definitely seems to be the case!

title: Excellent Wii Motion Plus Controller
text: I just purchased this Blue Wii Motion Plus Controller for use with my Wii U, and it seems to be workng great! I chose the Blue version only because it was a little bit cheaper price wise. Up until now, all of the previous Wii Remotes I have owned have been the older model "original" type of Wii Remote. So this is my first time trying a Wii remote that includes the Motion Plus feature. It seems to work very well and is very responsive! I am very pleased with it. I bought this controller because I needed a Wii remote which has the Motion Plus features in order to play certain games.

title: I am very Pleased with my Wii U!
text: I have owned a "normal" Wii for several years now. And I recently decided to purchase the Wii U, based on how much I had enjoyed many great games on my previous Nintendo system. Thus far I am loving my Wii U! I did a systems transfer of my old Wii game data, and everything went fine! So I am now playing all my old favorites on my Wii U, as well as looking forward to new games which will take advantage of the new system. The Nintendoland game which came with the deluxe set I purchased is loads of fun, and I would recommend the Wii U to anyone who has either owned or enjoyed a "regular" Wii. The new controller is fantastic and I can't wait to see what future games will be like!

title: Taking sound to the next level
text: Prior experience: First set of dedicated gaming earphones. Used with: PS3 - I don't have an Xbox360. Using the Quick Start Guide that was supplied, the cable connection part was easy enough, but the overall setup experience was a bit of a pain - first pairing the headset with the PS3 via Bluetooth, and then configuring the PS3. I didn't get any sound out of it at first (except for it telling me that it was powered on or politely saying goodbye) until it was fully charged, and then everything fell into place after that. It needs to be paired with the PS3 first as instructed or you cannot set it as your input/output device in the PS3 settings. There are three modes - game, movie and music. With game mode, you can choose from eight presets to enhance your gaming experience. There are also about eight presets for chatting, some of which can alter the sound of your voice. In addition, you can plug your headset into your computer and go to the Turtle Beach website (http://www.turtlebeach.com/community/preset-community) to customize the sounds of your favorite games to give yourself a competitive advantage, or to immerse yourself in the game through the use of audio presets and voice prompts. You will need to register to get access to the customization tools and to download Turtle Beach and Community created audio presets. The sound quality is excellent for game play, (for example, you can hear the footsteps of your opponents even before they come around a corner) as well as for chatting with other players while playing. In addition, the earphones are very comfortable for long hours of use and block out any surrounding noise. Another great feature is the Dolby surround sound. There are six easily accessible settings that you can use to get the effects to suit your current gaming mood. It takes about 6 hours to charge, but this is not a problem as you can continue playing while it is charging. The manufacturer states that a full charge lasts about 15 hours, but due to real life interruptions I have not been able to verify this. The headset can be paired via Bluetooth to two Bluetooth enabled devices simultaneously. For example, you can chat via your PS3 when playing a game and still receive/make phone calls, but I haven't tried the phone part as yet. There are separate Bluetooth volume controls on the right ear cup to adjust the chat/phone volume (Game volume controls are on the left ear cup) Finally, using the mobile device cable supplied, you can plug it into any regular earphone jack and the headset can now be used as regular earphones with your audio device (music/MP3 player, computer, tablet, smartphone, etc.) Overall, the sound is great and truly enhances your entire gaming experience.

title: D'oh, oh dear!
text: Let's start at the very beginning. If you're new to gaming, this is NOT a very good place to start. You're better off beginning with I, II, III Or you'll go directly to d'oh (and probably give up) The graphics are fantastic, and the settings and story line imaginative. There are new weapons, skills, maps, characters and modes, but unfortunately the controls are confusing beyond my comprehension (my fault entirely, I'm sure) Loaned to a friendly (and mature) teenager who had prior experience with the game, it came back a couple of days later with rave reviews about Ezio defying Templars in the hunt for an ancient library in Constantinople using hookblades and bombs (or words to that effect) Not for the uninitiated, but from all reports this is a challenging game for skilled gamers, and well worth the time spent to master it. Amanda Richards, December 3, 2012

title: A big bundle of unnecessary clutter
text: Adjective: Not necessary: dispensable, inessential, needless, nonessential, uncalled-for, unessential, unneeded, unrequired Add: Superfluous Redundant And: Fugeddaboudit I thought that this would have been a fun accessory set for the Wii Sports package, but on reflection, I should have used the money towards an additional controller or nunchuck instead. 1. The pieces don't fit together well, and it requires some patience to get the threads to line up properly. 2. The base that holds the controller feels flimsy, and if you use too much force to unscrew the attachment, it'll probably break. 3. The base is uncomfortable for small hands, especially for the baseball grip. 4. You lose the vibration effect 5. In baseball, you have to take the controller out of the handle to pitch, or else look rather silly pitching with a bat in your hand. It doesn't take long, but it's something you don't need to do if you're not using the accessory. 6. You'll need to take the controller out of the padded sleeve before using these accessories. (And then put it back on when you're through) The bottom line is that these accessories add nothing to the Wii Sports experience, and you're much better off keeping things simple and using the regular remote controller on its own. Amanda Richards, March 7, 2009

title: Oh, my achin' agin' anteriors!!
text: Santa dropped this off at our house the other day, and I'm pretty sure he had a smile on his ruddy face when he did it. "I'll teach those bleedin' couch potatoes", he said with a laugh. "Ho Ho Ho", and off the old jelly belly flew, with his sleigh full of Wii related accoutrements for sedentary families around the world. Having the good fortune to have a semi-geek in the house, the Wii thing was soon set up in the kid's bedroom, and after 5 hours I thought I should check on the adult kid and the little kid - just in case. Santa had sadistically included an extra controller and nunchuk with the package, so added to the pair that comes with the set, a full scale 2 kid war was in progress, covering bragging rights for five included games - boxing (little kid leading), bowling (big kid ahead), baseball (no clear advantage - but then we don't play baseball here, because it's just not cricket), tennis (neither will see Wimbledon) and golf (Tiger's safe for now) They had set up a Mii (avatar) for each member of the family (self included), and looking at the body shape they chose for me, I immediately remembered that I should make a New Year resolution to lose weight. Soon enough a challenge was issued, and hours later I emerged as the household bowling champion, but threatening to sue for physical abuse for my boxing loss. (I think they made it personal) All these games have an aerobic and physical element, and if you don't get yer lazy azz in gear, nothing much happens. Bowling for instance, requires you to swing the controller like you would a bowling ball (making sure that you secure it around your wrist first so you don't put a hole in your TV), and after hours of unaccustomed exercise, your muscles can really feel the burn. And it's not only your arm muscles. One does not bowl without the correct body language after all. Oh the pain!! Now they're looking at all the other doo-dads and wing-dings to further their Wii experience, and making strong birthday and father's day hints. IMHO they should drop off their requests to the fat man in the red suit, and get HIM to come over and play some games. Off to review some Icy Hot and Radian B, and make a massage appointment. Amanda Richards, December 28, 2008

title: RIP tangled cords
text: PS2 users and the people who live with them can breathe a sigh of relief after buying this cordless controller. Installation is so easy that anyone who can read Basic English can complete it in minutes, including reading time and putting in the two AA batteries which are included in the package. Quadruple your time if you're counting the time it takes to open the tightly sealed packaging as this may require the use of power tools. (Slight exaggeration) After releasing the controller from bondage and putting in the batteries the right way, simply plug the receiver into the slot where the old wired controller used to be, and you're good to go. My son, the resident expert, reports better control, better feel and better buttons, and I guess he likes it because he disappeared with it into his room, and we've had a peaceful day since then. Instead of sitting up close to the TV, he can now sit way back on the bed in royal comfort, and best of all, I know I won't be risking my neck tripping over wires as I pass through the war zone. Another thing that I can say is majorly cool and improved is the vibration feature. I received permission to hold it and push a few buttons during a game, and this feature really put me in the game. After being rescued from peril by an exasperated child, I retired hurt, but very pleased with this controller. Two minor cons are keeping track of the controller without using a tracking device or bloodhound, and having to change the batteries every 45-50 hours of playing time. No biggies. Amanda Richards, December 25, 2008

title: Works with Linux
text: I was leery of buying this mouse as I have a Razer keyboard that has been the least reliable keyboard I've ever owned. Fortunately, this mouse has been a stellar performer. I'm on month 3 of using the mouse with Bluetooth and am at 79% battery capacity with the original battery. I work in IT, so I'm using this thing all day, and I try to remember to switch it off, although this doesn't always happen. I haven't used it for gaming yet, but I'll be using 2.4Ghz for sure. I tried this with 4 different Linux distros (Bluetooth) and hadn't had an issue so far. I tried the dongle out as well and had no problems.

title: Better options in Windows than Mac
text: The headset I bought from Amazon didn't come in a box and was very much used, regardless of me paying full price for a new set. Fortunately, I was able to return it for a full refund and bought it from OfficeMax at a much lower price. Since there are a lot of reviews out there, I'll make this quick: Pros: * Clear sound. * Works as intended. * The mute LED is super useful. Indifferent: * Will pair to multiple bluetooth sources, as long as you manually disconnect and connect it at the sources. * Bluetooth volume is adjusted by clicking the volume button down and going through the menu. Cons: * The headset will automatically disconnect from the PC, but will not reconnect without turning the headset off and on again, while bluetooth has no auto-disconnect/off feature. There may be a way to reactivate the connection to PC because the headset never really turns off, as it'll make the powerdown sound if I actually turn the headset off. I'll have to find out if I'm just using this feature incorrectly. * I get some distortion/buzzing with bass in certain circumstances, notably when watching some YouTube content, but fiddling with the equalizer seems to mitigate this. * Range isn't as good as I was expecting, and bluetooth doesn't always make a solid connection when reconnecting, as my coworkers said that I sounded like a robot when I left the room and came back. * If you wear these around your neck, be prepared for them to be uncomfortably snug, and the mute button to turn on and off while it rubs against your chest. * I was expecting deeper bass, but it performs decently well. * Battery life isn't the greatest in comparison to newer stuff out there, and the battery saving options are almost non-existent. I haven't read the manual and only had to go online for a couple things I couldn't figure out, but it has been working great so far. It's a great headset, although I'd prefer better battery life while also foregoing the swapping battery "feature". I bought this headset for work and play, pairing to my work laptop via bluetooth and my gaming laptop via the dock. I've found that the audio options in the GG application are a bit different between Windows and Mac. On Mac, you only get an equalizer with presets, volume limiter, live mic preview, and mic sidetone adjustment. On Windows, you 'also' get DTS 7.1 surround, surround profile, stereo profile, bass enhancement, and dialogue enhancement. I suspect this is due to licensing, and to be honest, I these extras don't do a whole lot, IMHO.

title: Wondrous!
text: This is TRULY grand! I've been waiting for 5 years, for Microsoft to get their butts in gear & stroke this original xbox game for the XBOX360...and I was just about to buy a used console to be able to play it. BUT, I took this chance on this PC version. Got a fright when, after installing this on my Windows 7 rig, I did get an error message telling me that it wouldn't be compatible...BUT that it would tweak itself a tad. Viola!, it instantly began-to-work...even recognizing the joy-stick and calibrating it! The game is hugely entertaining and vivid, in an arcade way...although you CAN adjust the experience to a more realistic handling environment. I'll have to "grow a few", first, before I do so. And THAT will not be easy as I am a gal.

title: Nice clarity of sound, multiple tips work with small ears.
text: Because I have small ears, I typically don't bother with ear buds, preferring to use Bluetooth headphones that cover the physical ear. Most ear buds are too big and cause pain within minutes or just fall out. Since this set comes with multiple bud sizes, I decided to try one more time. I've used these several times over the past few days with my LG V10 phone and two different Fire tablets. The plug is tight and there's no feedback or static listening to music or a video. The cord is long enough to comfortably have your device on your lap or in a pocket, but it isn't so long that it becomes unwieldy or tangle prone. The sound is surprisingly good and crisp with rock, country and even classical music. The different ear buds are for treble and base enhancement, depending on your desire. Nonetheless, the smallest set (clear in color) for treble fits my ears without falling out or pinching. The little carry pouch is exactly the right size to stash in my purse or carry on luggage. Since these actually fit me and sound good, I will be able to use these rather than a headphone style while doing dressage schooling (horseback riding). That's a pretty nice improvement in my daily life.

title: Substantial feel, perfect bedtime light
text: I got this lighted case for my Kindle Keyboard and it fits perfectly. I had been using another brand cover with the slide in pocket for the Kindle, but no light. The Amazon brand cover is heavier, feels more substantional all around actually. Insallation was easy - the little hooks clicked right into place on the side of the Kindle with a single try. The light slides out of the top right corner and lights up about 95% of the Kindle face. It's a pretty strong little light and makes it possible to read comfortably in an otherwise dark room. One thing I did like immediately was that the light doesn't spill out - my husband can sleep while I read without disruption. Definately glad I splurged and bought the lighted cover.

title: Difficult for newbies, great graphics and storyline
text: First thing - this game is really difficult for newbies to the gaming world. As adults with our first game system, we purchased several games in different genres for our new Wii system. We bought one of the other Resident Evil titles and loved it, so this one seemed like a natural choice due to the rave reviews and the first person shooter perspective. I love the graphics here - it's very easy to get sucked into the world and the feel of the game without question. Especially if you have the opportunity to set it up on a Hi-Def large screen television - gorgeous. However, this is a hard game! It's not a game for beginners unless you just enjoy frustration and shrieking at the tv and starting over again and again and again. The little tricks and subtle ins and outs that long time gamers all pick up as they play game after game after game hours on end seem to be needed and assumed for Resident Evil 4. That in and of itself is not a dealbreaker, just something I wish I had known ahead of time - I would have waited and purchased this game later on. What ended up happening is we got frustrated and stuck at the first village, stopped playing the game for a couple of months, conquered some others, learned some gaming tricks in general and have now come back to Resident Evil 4 with a fresh perspective and attitude and we're enjoying it much more the second time around. So.... not a game a for first timers, but one worth playing when you've gotten your feet wet elsewhere first.

title: Adults Playing on Wii - LOVE this Game!
text: My husband and I bought a Wii on a whim a month ago and bought 10 games in several genres to go with it. With no kids we're flying by our pants here when it comes to picking games - it's been a 50/50 proposition finding great games vs duds. This "Call of Duty - World at War" has turned out to be a great game! Both of us play this one alone and together at the same time and we've been having a blast with it either way. The story line is engaging, the graphics are excellent on a large high def television, we've definately found ourselves laughing at the humor (maybe inappropriately, but who cares, it's a GAME!) and laughing at each other as we play through the campaigns, the difficulty level is about right for first time gamers. We're challenged, but not to the point of frustration or watching my husband fling the Wii out a window. One of things I really like is that we can play together at the same time with two targets on a single screen - no split screens here. One hint - We did buy the smaller pistol type guns to use with this one rather than the big Wii Zapper contraption which really makes the game so much better! When we conquer this one, we'll definately move on and buy the next verson of the "Call of Duty" game.

title: LOVE this game - great graphics, fascinating to play
text: My husband and I bought a Wii on a whim after Thanksgiving and 7 different games to get us started. We bought games in a variety of genres so we could get a real feel for the system & figure out what we really enjoy. After trying a couple of other shooting games with the Wii pistol attachment for the Wii Remotes, "Dead Space Extraction" is the winner! This game is by far the best of all the games we've tried, including those that are not in the shooting categories. The graphics are amazing, the story line was quick-paced, made sense and the story actually had us wanting to know more. We loved being able to play side by side on a single screen without having to do the whole split screen effect - each of us has our own cross-hairs to aim and shoot the aliens with, but on one screen so we can make full use of the 50" television. The other nice thing about this game was that the main characters change without losing the flow of the story and the point of the game - keeps things interesting and stirs up the skill set. There are multiple difficulty levels here as well so when you think you've mastered it, you can come back and let it kick your butt all over again. SO GLAD WE BOUGHT THIS ONE!

title: Not the best Atelier game, unfortunately :/
text: I'm such a fan of Atelier! But this one is the game I like the least. The story is fun and enjoyable, and the characters are pretty neat. That said, there are several annoying things with the game. For starters, if you leave your home and go to the shop to sell an over-abundance of items, you have to have the items in your basket. So that means making SEVERAL trips between your home and shops. That might not sound so bad to you, but you have no idea... if you forget to sell your needless items, your inventory will cap out, and you'll be forced to pick and choose, then run back and forth selling. It's so tedious, and I swear I can feel myself getting older during it. This IS a good game, though!

title: Meh
text: My friend has one of these, and he convinced me to get it, insisting it would make typing easier. I don't like it... for me, it make typing harder. The buttons are tiny and glossy, so my fingers are constantly hitting the wrong keys. My other complaint is that it also made my controller much heavier, so every time I set the controller down to rest, the L2 and R2 buttons would get pressed (depending on what game you're playing, this can be seriously annoying). Don't let my review stop you from giving it a try, if you still want it. My friend absolutely loves it, and says it's flawless.

title: I got what I expected, and honestly enjoyed it.
text: Chulip, from its pictures alone, is obviously a game with bad graphics. However, I'm not one to judge a game on its graphics alone. I liked the idea of a 'kissing RPG', and wanted to try it out! Voices: My god, what in the hell are they saying? They didn't bother re-dubbing voices. They repeat the same lines over and over, which won't make sense to you at all, while text appears on the bottom of the screen. This was a small annoyance that I quickly got used to. What I loved was the challenge of gaining all those kisses. For everyone's information: ALL available kisses in the game are listed in the manual that come WITH the game, and even explains how to gain them. There's no need to buy or look up a guide. I felt a sense of triumph when I gained all kisses! It wasn't easy, and I did have a LOT of fun. This game is cheap used, and I highly recommended it for someone looking for an inexpensive challenge.

title: One of the most beautiful games I've ever played!
text: This game is a side scroller, with beautiful anime graphics, and excellent voice acting. It's set during a war, in which many sad things take place. Although there is a heavy level of sadness to this game, all-in-all it can have a happy ending if you play it right. One of my favorite things, is how classic fairy-tales are incorporated into this game. Beauty and the Beast, Red Riding Hood, Sleeping Beauty, The Blue Bird of Happiness, and much more. One tip I will give is this: Never throw food away. If you have no room in your bag for food you find, make room by eating the extra. Eating is what increases your HP!

title: Works just fine
text: We were in need of a replacement Wii controller after one of ours decided to bite the dust. It had been a long time since we bought a new controller. We tucked in new batteries and tried unsuccessfully to get this new controller to be acknowledged by our Wii. Over and over. We left out one step, long forgotten! There is a tiny red "sync" button located just below the batteries. You have to push it along with the sync button on your Wii base. Funny how it started working just fine after that! Ha ha! So, the remote works just fine. Just don't forget that tiny sync button step.

title: What a great series!!
text: I love to play games of all kinds, but many of the DS games are just not my style. (I am one of the few people around that don't really care for Mario, I suppose! Jumping for coins or mushrooms just isn't my thing.) This game is absolutely crammed with brain teasers. Nothing that would take a PhD to solve, and they vary in difficulty from easy to super hard. The difficulty is rated in "picarats", the point system the game uses. Like other Layton games, there is a mystery to solve. However, this one had a lot more to do than the Curious Village game. There are extra games in Layton's "trunk", and you have to find ingredients to brew various teas. In the course of the game you will come across characters that are thirsty and really want a nice cuppa tea of some sort. It will be your job to brew what they want. If you serve the right one, it will unlock yet another puzzle. I finished Curious Village completely in about 16 hours of play time. (I wasn't rushing, but still wasn't all that hard.) So far, I have been playing for about 22 hours, and still not completed. This is just more fun. You can keep going back to places you've already been to, and there will be another puzzle. There is also a place to collect pieces of a camera that was "dropped". Once you reassemble the camera, there are several places where you can take a "photo". That is yet another part of the game - you then compare the real scene with the photo you took, and spot three differences. If you get them all (per photo and there are 12), it unlocks yet another puzzle. I really truly love this series, and hope they continue to make them every year. I can hardly wait for the next two. These are a little pricey, but honestly, they are worth it. Lots of fun game play. All the puzzles are woven into a storyline that involves a lot of characters to solve the mystery. If you like brain teasers or even puzzles like Hi-Q, get this game. You won't be sorry.

title: More match 3 games
text: Well, I got this one because I thought it might be another level of fun or some other sort of goals. I had the Athens game and wanted to see how this one went. First off, my game was faulty. Since I had already left a review for the seller (that I apparently cannot change) and had the game for a while before I played it, I guess I am stuck. Many of the sidebar bonus items don't work - they only show up as a half an item, or just sit there, without being able to drag them to the game. But overall, getting back to the game alone, it is just another one of the games that you drag/swap to make matches of three or more like items. You buy/build your port city while you progress through the levels. Many of the levels are a little hard to see because of the small icons and the color combinations (like blue items on a blue background). The "cure" for this issue is to restart that level 0 it shuffles and you'll get a different color screen. Overall, my rating is "eh". I would not buy it again, and don't think all that much of the game.

title: it is too bad no one could write a manual
text: Well, this game was kind of fun, even if only for the challenge of completing a level. I have now finished level 100 and "been accepted as one of the gods" (per the game). The game was fun enough. It is a standard make-a-match-of-at-least-three icons. The things are kind of small (at least for my eyes), and I wished I could enlarge the game! When the chains are over the icons, you can barely make out what it is. I had to go by the colors. That being said, the documentation that comes with the game is THE PITS. It tells only the most basic information, things you automatically know if you have ever played any sort of electronic game. The game itself has a few notes that show up as a pop-up screen while you are playing. It is okay if you memorize everything, but I know I couldn't do it all! My biggest complaint is that the MANUAL should tell you what all those bloomin' power-ups on the side actually do! It doesn't. When you use one, it moves so quickly, you can't really tell what it did. I finally got it that the globe-type ball will destroy something like 11 tiles around whereever you place it. The hourglass gives you an unknown additional amount of time to complete the level. The rest? I don't know - they go too fast - I can't follow them. The flame burns some icons up, but which ones? I don't know. The purple globe does something, but no clue what. And on it goes... So, using them strategically is really hard! I think a game is a lot more fun when it is explained thoroughly so I know what the goal actually is - not a random stab at completion. I am in the process of going through the game again under a diff ID to write things down as the screens pop up. Seriously, how hard would that have been for the developers to do?!? Basic documentation of the game, and it is missing. It was okay, but never pay a huge amount for the game, and know that it is going to be a stab in the dark the first time through.

title: I really like this controller - it feels good in your hands.
text: I am not the video game expert in our house, but I have it on good authority that these are great! This is the second one of the iGlow controllers we have purchased. The first one was the black iGlow. Note that for some reason, the iGlow controllers come packaged in a box that uses magnets as the closure. Just a heads-up so you do not put the boxes near items in your room that might be sensitive to magnetic fields, such as computers or possibly stereos. No clue why they did not use Velcro, but I guess someone gave them a great deal on magnets! Both controllers use blue LED lighting to create a nice visual effect while playing. It makes playing games in a dark room a lot better! I've included a photo of both the white and the black together so you can see the differences. It looks to me like the same basic light, but the black vs white crackle effect gives a very different look to it all. They have a great feel to them, and the lights just make it all better. We use them with a Playstation 2. So far, we have not experienced any lag or other problems with the game play. I saw that a lot of the other reviews said this model broke easily. We have not experienced that, but we don't have little children - ours are older. Perhaps it is the care of the controller that makes it last better? We haven't had anything break in the time we've been using it. We've had ours since December 2010 without any problems. We don't toss it in a drawer though - we have a plastic storage bin that the controllers go in to. I could see it being easy to break if it was tossed onto something hard. Other than that - ours is going strong. All in all, highly recommended!

title: GREAT looking controller!
text: Well, this controller is completely worth getting. The blue color is amazing. We've only had it a little while, so I don't know how long it will last. However, this is my son's current favorite controller. The glow part is very bright, and makes it easy to see all the buttons while playing in the dark. I have to admit that this is one amazing-looking thing! All thumbs up as far as appearance. After he has used it a little while longer, I'll add his comments about the performance. Meanwhile - love it. Wish I had one in green for Mom! UPDATE: We have now purchased the RED Lava Glow as well. Both of the controllers look great while playing in a darkened room. No complaints of any kind so far on either button response or durability. But then, the users in our house are older, not little kids, so maybe little ones are rougher on them. We enjoy all of the specialty controllers we've purchased here on Amazon. We have both red and blue lava glow, as well as the white and the black iGlow. GREAT controllers that make the game better somehow.

title: John Deere should have done a better job!
text: Well, I got this for my JD-obsessed, former-farmer husband who is finally learning to use a computer. First off, he said that his computer came with a demo mode of this game, and he didn't care much for it. Who knew? He never mentioned it, and I was happy to find a JD game. I liked the looks of the graphics. So, he installed the game anyway and gave it a shot. It works better on Win7 than Vista or XP. I do agree that the first several levels are boring as all get out. You simply harvest - back and forth. The controls are NOT intuitive - it uses weird keys for forward, backward, etc, instead of the arrow keys. He didn't like that at all, and in fact, found it very uncomfortable to use the keyboard to play. That didn't stop him, as he was trying to get to a certain level. There are places in the game where you can see unusual things (like a fire in the field?), but going over to them does not tell you what they are, how to fix it, what to do, etc. There's nothing in the manual that he saw, so it is just a smoking pile of mystery out there in the field. I guess someone dropped a cigarette or lightning struck while he was plowing over a few rows! All in all, I expected a LOT more from a game with John Deere on the label. We all know they charge enough for their licensed products! They should do some quality control too. I can't recommend this one. If he continues to play and changes he mind, I'll update the review. Until then, feel free to try another game. This has a great package but awkward and sometimes boring play.

title: I realize I'm in the minority here, but ...
text: ... I really didn't care for this all that much. A few of the games are kind of fun, but it's not enough to turn me into a fan. My first issue with Brain Age 2 is the first challenge: it guides you to use "Rock, Paper, Scissors" to assess brain age. That's all well and good if you know how to play the game, but I've never played it in my life (I'm no youngster, either). Maybe it just wasn't popular where I grew up -- I don't know. But I had no idea how to play it. You start the program, it asks you if you are in a place where you can speak without telling you what's ahead, you say "yes," and there you are in the middle of "Rock, Paper, Scissors." And no where do they give you the rules, either in the program itself or in the instruction/info booklet. How am I supposed to know what it takes to "win" or "lose" if I've never played and don't know the rules? I mean, they give me "rock" and "win" or "scissors" and "lose," and I'm supposed to respond ... how???? It's not like the game actually makes any sense (I did finally go to wiki to see how it's played -- paper is stronger than rock? ?? that makes NO sense at all.) So that turned me off. I learned from that always to answer "NO" to the question about if I'm somewhere I can speak. Next, the little cartoon "Dr. K" guy is annoying. I mean REALLY annoying. Oh, not at first -- but deal with this guy for 4 days straight and his "humor" starts grating. Miss a day and you get a scolding. Getting the same "brain tips" day after day is getting really old, too. I enjoy the Piano Player challenge, the Change Maker challenge, and the "sign" challenge. That's about all. And I can't imagine that playing these once a day will do anything to increase my brain power which, according to my first score based on my pitiful performance with RockPaperScissors, is realllly old. (In all fairness, when I took the "alternate" brain age assessment tests, I did much better, but still ... ) Word Blend seems to test your hearing more than your brain power: you hear two words pronounced simultaneously, and you're asked to write in both words given one or two letters. I tried this with and without earphones, and found no difference in my ability to discern two separate words from the mumble presented. Anyway, if you like disembodied heads bobbing around making faces, and games that are a mixed bag in terms of enjoyment, you might like Brain Age 2. If not, you might want to look elsewhere.

title: Fun little game, even for us "older folks" ...
text: I'm relatively new to the Nintendo DS Lite (and video-based games in general), having just received the unit at Christmas, but I'm getting a lot of enjoyment out of it. As a kid, I always loved the "find the object in the picture" puzzles in various children's magazines. Nothing has changed much! As a much older adult (ahem!), I still get a kick out of scrutinizing a picture to try to find various "hidden" objects. This particular game would probably would be suitable for someone 10 yrs old and up. Some of the clues may need explanation for younger kids ("ocean predator," "Roman 10," etc.). The artwork in this game is very nice. And I really like the fact that, from the very beginning, you're tasked with finding tiny relatively obscure objects as well as larger more obvious ones. As you progress through the levels, the number of objects increases (as does the time to find them, to a point). But part of the task might be finding multiple occurrences of an "object" -- say, "3 bats" or "2 spider homes." And those bats? well, how many definitions are there for "bat"? Just be prepared to broaden your search to more than just *one* type of item. So, if you need to find 36 "objects," you may actually need to locate closer to 45 or so, depending on the number of multiples you're asked to locate. This makes it more interesting, in my view. As you finish a level, you're offered another kind of puzzle to solve: word search, jigsaw puzzle, mah johng, tile rotate -- none of which are very difficult. The story? Well, basically, there's a narrative/text story that sort of runs along in the background, but seems to have little to do with the objects you're asked to find. Your "locations" are all in the town where the alleged art theft occurred, but beyond that, they play little role in your activities, other than to serve as the backdrops for your seek-and-find activities. At no time are you asked to try to solve the crime -- in fact, the culprit and plot are all laid out for you, seemingly disjointed from the puzzles. You simply solve the puzzles. That's it. Eventually, you finish by getting through all the levels and finding the items you're asked to find. Still, it's a beautifully rendered game, and I'll probably play it again. The only other game like this I have is "Mystery Case Files: MillionHeir" -- they're very similar, but I probably like "Mystery P.I.: Portrait of a Thief" a little better, mostly due to the art and the variety of the other puzzles.

title: I do not like it.
text: This is very hard to play or understand how to play. I am 37 and not that great with gaming systems but I can normally understand it later. There are so many things going on my 8 year old gave up on it and I tried to figure it out for him. I was so excited to get a Nintendo Switch but so far I do not like the two games I got. I go this one and Mario Kart and even though I love Mario Kart its boring after a while. The graphics are amazing on this one but it truly is hard to tilt the screen, move the joysticks, and press buttons all at the same time and having to reset your point of view constantly. I guess a professional gamer may have better luck but I can't say I like this game at all.

title: Good quality, but key spacing too tight.
text: Bought this keyboard to replace first gen G15 which I spilled a mixed drink into. I was rather disappointed, mainly because they crunched in the key spacing to fit in the extra macro keys on the left. The keys spacing is unbearably tight! Also there is no USB ports on this model. Returned item and went with Logitech G110 and am glad I did (better key spacing, USB port. No LCD screen but it's not a big deal). I will say that the G series quality is still there with this item. If the key spacing doesn't scare you, I'd recommend it.

title: Great mouse, buggy software
text: Well, the mouse is great, and so far I prefer it over Razer mice I've had in the past. I'm taking 1 star off because of the buggy, laggy software. It runs slightly better if you run with admin privileges, but it's still buggy and laggy. Changes don't take effect immediately the way they do in Razer software. The UI is also not very intuitive. If you will never need to use the software, then you can consider this a 5 star review. Just remember that it's a gaming mouse. It's not going to last forever. If you game frequently, expect to replace it in 1-2 years.

title: these are amazing. The price and the sound quality together make ...
text: Wow, these are amazing. The price and the sound quality together make these one of the best headsets I've ever owned. Make sure you install the software, though. That makes all the difference. I keep these puppies on the Hi-Fi setting most of the time, but the "Movie" and "Music" settings are both nice. As far as longevity, I can't say. But I will update this review down the road. For the price, though, I say go ahead. UPDATE: Today, after around 6 months, the cord broke. Well, more specifically, I broke the cord. HOWEVER, I broke the cord trying to untangle it. That is the downfall of these headphones. The cord tangles something wicked. The cord is wrapped in cloth, which is nice, but it tangles in tiny loops that build up over days. So watch this very carefully. You have to de-tangle the thing every single day or you will get huge knots, and like me, you will probably end up pulling the cord right out of the headset trying to de-tangle it. So, for this, I felt I had to remove a star.

title: A decent game, but fans of the series will be disappointed (Spoiler free!)
text: They say evolution is a series of mistakes. In that sense, this certainly evolves the series. While some Final Fantasies have suffered from being too linear or having a slow, lethargic battle system, where you are constantly harassed by useless battles.. this one swings (for my taste) much too far in the opposite direction. They wanted open world, but the world almost feels TOO open.. I know that sounds a little silly, but the sidequests (of which there are many) feel almost pointless. You want to do them.. but there is so much travel time involved, that you may just wind up opting out. Which brings me to point 2 of the world being "too open". I've spent probably half of the 20 hours I have been playing the game so far as a passenger in a car or driving a car to a location. Sometimes you can "fast travel", but for some reason loading times seem almost as long as the 5 minutes of travel time. This is not a game you are going to play if you have 30 minutes to kill, because you probably aren't going to really get to do anything. The battle system is an absolute mess. Fans of the series... understand turn based battle is completely gone, as is major coordination with your party. You really only control your character and then some special moves for your party members. If you equip them with spells, they may cast them on you if you are in the wrong spot. 20+ hours in and I feel as if the battle system is little more than button mashing. The entire concept of strategy seems to be gone. You can change to (as I did) the "wait" battle mode, which is supposed to allow you to feel more turn based, but it doesn't really help. It lets you choose your personal next target, but that is about it. Often times you are fighting a dozen or more enemies at once and suddenly dozens of arrows appear on the screen and you just wind up thinking "whatever, I'll just keep mashing the O" Unlike other Final Fantasy games, this one almost seemed to be based in the real world, with only slight tweaks. They travel in a car, contact each other on cell phones. Yes, you have Daemons and such, but when you have to pull up to a gas station that looks exactly like a highway rest stop, you feel as if some of the fantasy is missing. One of the things I used to love about Final Fantasy was its ability to create whole new worlds that are only very loosely based on ours. This feels much more like they took our world and threw in a few tweaks to make it into a Final Fantasy game. (I know that is not how it evolved, but the final product has that feel). I get that they wanted the game to evolve.. but so many of these "evolutions" (Battle system, open world with endless travel time, based so close t the real world) feel like mistakes that will drive away long time fans and, for me, the story hasn't been engrossing enough to pull me in. I got this game on release day and have played it mostly on weekends, but this weekend, I realized I didn't touch it. I just didn't want to spend half my time watching scenery go by or deciding whether I want to bother with sidequests or just get on with the story... a story I don't feel invested in the way I did other FF. FF has been my go to game for close to 20 years now and whenever a new one comes out I tell my wife.. well, prepare not to see me for a while. Well.. that hasn't happened with FF XV. So, if you are like me and play this game to be taken away to a whole new world and engrossed in a story and enjoy the strategic combat from previous games? Rent it first and try it out before you buy it, because you may not like what you get!

title: A great game, that tries to break the mold (but probably shouldn't have).
text: This really is a fun game to play in many different ways, but they had several great ideas, that just didn't appear to be executed in the best possible way. Some of these are easily fixed... some are built into the game structure and make it less fun than it could be. On the PvE side of things, they have a fun and interesting storyline and LOTS to explore. Almost TOO MUCH too explore. In order to "complete" a map (which you get rewards for), you have to find every point of interest, every vista (a lookout point that you have to jump to), complete every quest, find every waypoint (travel spots), and earn every skill point. Those who love exploring, will, no doubt find this tons of fun. However, if you JUST follow your storyline, you quickly find that you wind up in areas far above your level, so it becomes in your best interest to either gain experience by completing the map OR finding another "starter zone" to do early quests. I am not a fan of being forced backwards before moving on and would rather the storyline flow more with your leveling, BUT they give you so many different ways to earn experience, that isn't so much of a drag that it brings you down. You also have "Dynamic events" that pop up and you can join in and help. (ie, minotaurs are invading and you need to help stop them). I wanted to add a little more in here, in regards to the "completion" of a map and something I learned which is both good and bad. When you "complete" a map, I mentioned you get rewards. Those rewards are geared to your level. So, if you complete maps as you go along you will get random rewards for your level, which likely aren't worth much, because you level very quickly... However, IF you don't finish anything and then wait until level 80 to complete the zones... THEN you get very valuable rewards. Nice for people who rushed through early and then decide to go back and find all the vistas and points of interest... kinda sucky for people who spent the time to fully explore their maps at the lower levels. There are 3 parts of the PvP world. First, there is tournament style Structured PvP, where your pre-made group of 5 faces off against another pre-made group. This can be fun, but quite annoying, as I will explain more below due to balance issues. Second, there is open PvP servers where you join a server and it randomly puts you on the red or blue team and you fight to control points. You may switch teams in the middle of a match, or from map to map. This is kinda fun, but again, due to some balance and mechanics issues I have with the game, not as fun as it could be. Then there is WvWvW (world v world v world), which is, by far, the most fun part of the game, where you join with your entire server to control points on a map and score points against other servers. Unfortunately, current queue times to get into WvWvW range from 3-5 hours, so, at the moment, getting in to play this aspect of the game is like winning the lottery. I am sure they will fix this will time, because that type of wait time is obviously unacceptable. So.. what are the problems? The dynamic events are too frequent and too repetitive. They are a really cool aspect of the game, but the novelty of them wears off quickly and you find yourself starting to ignore them after just a few hours of play. Worse, the same events pop up over and over and over again in the same spots. One particularly annoying one is right by the crafting stations and it won't let you craft until the "event" is over and it seems as if every time I hop over to craft, the "event" is happening. My biggest complaint with the game that won't change and will frustrate many MMORPG gamers. They have done away with the "holy trinity" of Tank/Heals/DPS and given each class abilities to self heal, group heal, CC, tank, etc. There are some "tankier" classes and some that are more useful with group heals, but nothing like what you are used to. If you LIKED playing a healer or tank in previous games, you are likely to find GW2 quite frustrating... DPS is king here... You can put together some burst DPS builds that can bring down someone in seconds (or fractions of seconds), with little they can do about it. You have "control" and "support" roles, but in the end, a group of burst DPS thieves or life steal necromancers is going to roll over even the most skilled and "balanced" team. Which brings me to what I mentioned earlier about balance. "Build" is king in this game. Even though everyone in SPvP is boosted to level 80 and given access to all the same weapons and their full skill trees... Which weapons you choose, which skills you slot and which traits you boost will 95% determine your dominance in PvP... skill is secondary to build. Having the right build will overpower skill nearly every time. My friend linked me a burst dps warrior built which I created and within minutes was dominating in PvP only having to press 3 keys over and over again. Maybe to some people spending hours going over different combinations of skills/traits/weapons to come up with the one that gives you the highest crit chance, coupled with the most vitality and toughness seems like fun. However, I just want to PLAY the game. So, yes, it is great that the give you lots of choices and the ability to create your own role, but I don't see any way they are every going to achieve true balance, there is going to be a constant flux of nerfing and buffing. In the build up to the game and interviews, this seemed to be exactly what they were trying to avoid, but maybe it is just an inevitability with MMORPGS?
