So at the end of the day... it is a really fun game, but not without some serious flaws some of which are part of the design and some which will likely never be completely fixed.

title: A good game that tries to break the mold (but probably shouldn't have)
text: This review is based on the final beta weekend, which after playing I decided to go ahead and pre-purchase, but the game is not without some flaws, yet it is far FAR better than other recent offers in this genre (The Secret World I am looking in your direction!). The graphics are well done and you really get a good sense of an immense world... it ALMOST felt too big and the directions you could go were fairly limitless. The questing system was one of the better ones, as it gave you enough guidance to get you where you needed to go, but not so much that it was holding your hand. Further, you felt free to pursue whatever quests you wanted without being forced in a particular direction. The game makes use of dynamic events, which is a little similar to rift, in that SOMETHING happens nearby and asks all nearby players to work towards a common goal. These are often helpful in also completing your quests. However, on the downside, I felt they relied on the dynamic events a little TOO MUCH, as it seemed one was popping up every 5 minutes, making them quickly become less of a special thing and more common place. Spacing them out more (maybe 1 or 2 per hour) would make them feel more special. Withing a few hours of questing, I was starting to ignore the onscreen notification of "an event is taking place nearby". I really liked the PvP systems they developed for this game. First you have an arena style pvp zone, where you automatically get pumped up to top level, given all your skills and given the high end gear for your character. There are several different "capture the flag" style zones that you can jump right into and start pvp'ing as soon as you get into the game. In this same zone they also have tournament PvP, where you can get together with a pre-made group and battle other pre-made groups in the same zones. ( I spent most of my time during this beta in this zone so I could get an idea of the full capabilities of all the classes and once I got my grove, it was a blast!) Secondly in PvP you have a WvWvW (world v world v world) system in which your entire server battles against other servers for dominance by capturing forts and key points on a map from one another. This really adds a added bonus to the game in that you feel a greater sense of purpose in joining with people on your own server to work together towards a common goal. There is no need to party up or join a raid, but you can still join in the battle and work together. For me, the biggest negative, and the only reason I give this game only 3 stars is that in a decision to "break the mold" of MMORPGs the developers decided to do away with the "holy trinity" of DPS/TANK/HEALER and rather make each class self-sufficient. While I completely appreciate the thought, I don't think it quite worked out the way they planned and it seemed to do more to frustrate gameplay a little bit. While I agree that the idea of "needing a healer" or "needing a tank" to complete a raid or form a team needs to change, trying to completely eliminate these roles really diminishes the fun for people (like me) who flat out LIKE playing the healer or tank. This is where I felt The Secret World had a great idea (keep the basic dynamic, but allowing a character change professions on the fly), but they screwed up the questing system so much they made the game unplayable. So.. if you are someone who likes playing a healer or a tank, this game will be a little frustrating, because the playstyle you have become used to isn't supported here. Further, it seems that while they eliminated "traditional" roles, class makeup still seemed to play a HUGE role in who won matches. Two Guardians (the closest they have to a "tank class" could essentially act as a single tank for an entire party (by chaining their conditional removal and regeneration efforts, they become almost unbeatable) and Warriors, when paired with elementalists, could deliver HUGE burst DPS through combinations... so while the stated goal of not having a healing class or a tank class was to remove the necessity of particular group make ups, there is STILL the necessity of group make ups if you want to win matches. In short, while each individual class is nicely balanced against each other (no one class is really OP), group makeup still plays the primary role in how you will succeed and if you don't have the right class composition, you are going to lose your match, thus undermining the entire reason they eliminated the "holy trinity" to begin with. While these are problems with the game play, it is still a fun game with lots of potential. For a "beta" it seemed EXTREMELY polished and ready to go. I am looking forward to seeing the final release.

title: Not what it promises to be.
text: This is a game that had a TON of potential, but completely missed the mark. I was extremely excited for all that this game promise.. This game promises No Classes, No Levels, Total Freedom of Play...the reality of the game is quite different. I think everyone understood there was some wiggle room in their marketing statements, as there would be some type of progression and "leveling", which there is. Instead of the traditional leveling, you earn Skill Points and Ability points and apply them to a "skill wheel", which unlocks different skills for different weapons. This ultimately allows for a single character to take on any role in the game.. wanna be a tank, switch weapons, wanna be a healer, switch weapons, so the only real reason to create an "alt" is to join a different faction or for cosmetic purposes. Unfortunately, where the game goes horribly wrong is in the forced progression curve, which winds up being far more restrictive and linear than many of the other MMORPG's I played (including SWTOR, which had a very linear and specific storyline to follow). The usual MMO experience is you move into a zone, pick up all the quests, do the quests, gain experience "clear" the zone and then move onto the next, harder zone. Some people choose to focus on one quest at a time, some people follow a specific storyline, and some people grab everything in place and grind through quests as fast as possible... Secret World is NO DIFFERENT in set up. If you do not clear most of the zone, you will not be powerful enough to move onto the next zone. However, unlike other MMO's, Secret World restricts HOW you go through the zone and forces you to constantly backtrack in a forced time sink. In The Secret World, you accept mission A from character A. On the way to your objective you encounter character B who requests you also to complete a task at the same place. You go to accept this new missions thinking "cool, I can kill two birds with one stone" and you get a warning window that you must "pause" quest A to accept quest B. If you choose to pause quest A and take quest B, you have to go back to character A to "unpause" quest A, leaving you to run back and forth over the same ground several times... and it isn't just character A and B, you come across character C, D, E, F and G along the way and each time you talk to them you are told you can't accept their missions without abandoning the mission you are on... Freedom of play? Why can't I get BOTH bandages and medication from the pharmacy at the same time?? No, I have to get the bandages, return them to character A, then find character D again, go back to the same pharmacy and find the medication and return it to character D and then hunt out character B who wanted water from the store which was right next to the pharmacy. The developers have offered several conflicting excuses for this baffling limitation, everything from "memory problems on the backend" to it being a high level decision made to force you to get immersed in each mission, instead of treating characters like mission hubs. Ultimately, one honest dev admitted that if they removed the limitation it would break the progression curve and they would have to reduce the amount of experience you gained from each mission and people would complain there isn't enough content. (ie, we need to force you to run back and forth because you would progress through the game too fast if we allowed you to follow a logical progression.) This brings me back to the main selling point... "TOTAL FREEDOM OF PLAY" If I am someone who chooses to grind quests, why is there something wrong with that? If am someone who WANTS to focus on one quest at a time, great. If I want to do 3 at a time, why am I not allowed to make that choice? They made it 100% clear in the forums that this system was NOT up for debate and would NOT be changed under any circumstances. This non-intuitive questing system made the game feel like work, rather than fun. I was looking for a game that offered more freedom of gameplay and this felt exactly the opposite.

title: A great start with lots of potential - Potential failed... Cancelled my sub.
text: Leaving my previous review below, because it was written before patch 1.2 and what this game was to become, so you can read my original optimism! What ruined potential. Once you hit level 50, the game becomes an absolute mindless grind, with no sense of purpose at all. It is one thing to do the same raids over and over if they are fun or have purpose, but it loses its luster quickly and becomes the usual (stand on the x, hit the 3 key seven times, then the 5 key times and then stand on spot Y). The PvP (basically now reduced to warzones ONLY) have absolutely no sense of purpose, except to grind for gear. They are supposedly introducing "team" play, but they missed the opportunity to have a overall purpose to the PvP, such as helping your chosen FACTION. Open world PvP is non-existent and had no sense of purpose either. For a game that started off telling an amazing story... it completely loses its way towards the end and you just don't care about what happens anymore. Space combat.. great potential gone wrong. You wind up repeating the exact same space missions during your initial progressions. (The level 40 missions are the exact same as the level 20 missions, just with slightly higher goals (kill 40 fighters instead of 20). When they added content to the story in patch 1.2.. I didn't both to complete it as I had stopped caring about the storyline. It's a shame, because this could have been a fantastic game, but they took the easy way out and decided to turn it into a mindless grind. This is defiantly one of the better MMO's and has some aspects that make it much better than the rest. The Best Aspects: The story line is fantastic and the voice acting makes it much more enthralling than other games which simply present you with a wall of text. It maintains the feel of both an MMO and single player game. Crafting. Finally a game got this right. You don't have to spend endless boring hours grinding away at resource gathering and standing over a forge. You get companions in the game and send them on missions and they gather the resources for you and craft the items, earning you experience. This is the first MMO where I am actually doing the crafting. They have nice bonus systems to encourage you to group, but you don't HAVE TO if you don't want to in order to complete your story line. (If you group with others you earn experience from them completing quests as well as you own, so you level much faster!) The Good Aspects: Space combat is a lot of fun, but isn't fleshed out yet. You can do space missions, but are essentially stuck on a rail as your ship steers itself through space and you control where and what you shoot, with small room for movements. Characters are pretty customizable, as you can switch your skill tree. So you can go up the healing tree and then decide you want to do DPS and go back to your trainer and spend some credits to reassign your skills. (You get the first swap for free). You can also create interesting hybrid characters, who can serve dual purposes. What needs work: The PVP just isn't there yet. There isn't anything to encourage people into open world PvP, so it is pretty much restricted to "warzones". These are mini, repeatable instances where they put equal number of republic and empire and give them a goal to achieve. Great idea.. execution isn't there yet. There is no in game voice communication, so you get thrown into a random group and then it becomes difficult to execute because you can't communicate quickly. Further they put people of all levels into the same warzone and although they scale your HP up to level 50, unless you are level 50, your gear and skills aren't on par. (Hopefully they will bracket the warzones in the future to make them more balanced). Overall, however, this is a great game that has lots of potential. Hopefully they resist the urge to go with other MMO's have gone before them and just turn it into a constant grind for gear. Right now, it isn't grindy and that alone makes it worth playing!

title: Meh.. got really bored
text: I really liked Dragon Age Origins and wound up playing it multiple times through on different classes. I believe my gameplay time was 60 hours, mostly because I wanted explore every nook of the game. I just finished Dragon Age II this afternoon in 35 hours of playtime. I COULD have played longer, but was getting incredibly bored with doing the same types of quests in the same locations over and over again, so I ultimately chose to just head for the endgame and get it over with. With Dragon Age: Origins you had a sense of purpose and a goal you felt you were reaching for... In Dragon Age II you feel as if you are wandering about aimlessly doing quests for cash, because in reality that is what you are doing most of the time. [tiny spoiler in next paragraph] About 30% of the way into the game you feel as if you are finally breaking away from the city, when you join an expedition into the deep roads. I was excited when this part came up as I felt it was going to lead to the rest of the quest.. however, once you are done with the expedition, you go BACK to the city and start doing the repetitive questing again until the end of the game. After 30 hours, the game started to feel really "grindy", just doing stuff so you can gain levels.. cash.. and equipment. If I want to grind I will go play an MMORPG.. PS3 games shouldn't have these aspects as part of the basic gameplay. Now that I am done, I have no desire to go back and play again with a different strategy. Of the 35 hours I played... I'd say 30 of them were spent in the exact same locations doing the same thing. With the above said.. it is not ALL bad. The graphics were fantastic. The characters were interesting and fun.. especially the interplay between them. The fighting was ramped up a lot from the first version, making it a nice challenge at times and I was really enjoying it up until [same small spoiler about to happen] you wind up BACK in town after finally getting out of that place. Overall.. if you are just looking for the Dragon Age experience... it will fill that void. However, if you are looking for an epic storyline and lots of adventure... find something else. This will likely frustrate you more than you will enjoy it.

title: Doesn't live up to its expectations...
text: I am a huge fan of Roberta Williams, her King's Quest games have offered me hours of entertainment since I was about 9 years old. When I heard that she was taking on a more "adult" project featuring real actors and a gripping, horror-based storyline, I was more than excited. However, I received nothing but disappointment. The graphics in this game are most impressive (considering the time that the game was created). They feature real actors who are placed in front of a blue screen with a cartoon-ish backround and props projected behind them. This gives the game a fairly realistic effect although at times the actors look so out of place in front of their backrounds that the occuring event is everything but real. As far as the acting goes..it's about what you'd expect from a game which resembles a B horror movie. Most of the acting is barely believeable (although Adrienne, the main character, is not horrible) and the characters themselves are most annoying. The story was just awful...cliched and robbed to the core, I found absolutely everything in this game to be entirely predictable. It focuses around a couple, Don and Adrienne, who move into a huge, spooky house on an island. The house was owned by a creepy count named Carno and it is said to be haunted. All of the islanders are afraid of the house and none of them are too keen on talking about it (with the exception of one eager old woman who serves as the "revelation of the evil within" source seen in all movies of this sort). The story proceeds just as you would predict. Without giving anything away I'll just tell you that Adrienne discovers ghosts, secret rooms, and a demon which has been wreaking havoc on the house for years. It borrows heavily from Stephen King's "The Shining" (as in..the house turns the husband into a raving psychopath). For anyone who is not too familiar with the horror genre, Phantasmagoria may provide a few hours of good story. To fans of classic horror movies and games, Phantasmagoria will become stale before the end of chapter three. This brings me to the gameplay. The game itself is divided into 7 chapters (each chapter contained entirely on its respective disk). While this may seem as though it allows for a massive game, it must be said that each chapter can be completed in a quick half hour, even by the most inexperienced of adventure gamers. The puzzles that each chapter requires you to solve are completely lacking in challenge. They are solved by the use of obvious items in Adrienne's inventory and no logical thought is necessary. There was actually a chapter in the game which focused entirely on buying a bottle of Dran-O from the village general store and returning it to your husband. Yes - that's it. Later - a puzzle comes up where the very item you need can be found a single screen below and it is not hidden in the very least. To fans of blood and gore - this game may serve as an enjoyable "shockfest". There is more than one moment of senseless violence which is not limited to beheading, faces being ripped open, and the funneling of human body parts down a woman's throat. For those too squeamish to even imagine such things, the gore can easily be censored with an in-game option requiring the entry of a password (to protect the little ones' virgin eyes). Overall, Phantasmagoria lacks in every area required to make an adventure game reach "classic" status. The story is predictable, the gameplay simple and stale, and the characters annoying. For huge fans of senseless violence and B-movie horror plots, this may serve as some sort of "cult classic" piece. All others, don't waste your money.

title: Simplistic and monotonous
text: The graphics look great and on my upper mid-range system it runs fine. Well, except for frequently crashing or just ceasing to respond. Everything else about this game is simplistic as if made for a 5 year old who needs to be led around and told what to do. Also, the endless droning voiceovers will make you want to defect and join the other side just so you don't have to hear the dull, monotonous voices over and over and over and over. And then there is steam which can and does ruin every game it touches. The CODEX version actually runs better for me. Wait until you can buy this on sale for 10 bucks before wasting money on it.

title: Decent Keyboard, Horrible Software
text: This keyboard is nice enough for the price. It has a good touch for typing and the red lighting shows up surprisingly well. What isn't nice is the programming software. In fact, it's some of the worst I've ever seen. They put almost no effort into it and the result is difficult, tedious and barely useable. If you're very interested in programming macros, get a logitech. I haven't tried the razor software so can't speak to it, but this software is much harder to program with than logitech's and even a bit worse than cooler master's. Example: The worst part of the software is once you have programmed in and edited your macro, you cannot save it. It is forever bound to the key you selected. If you decide you want it on a different key, you have to program it into that key. With the logitech software, once you have created a macro you can drag and drop it whereever you want. So as not to be all about talking up logitech I will say physically I like this keyboard better than any logitech I've used. And I've used quite a few.

title: Impressive
text: "Wow," is the best I can think of to say about this game. It's really something and I like it a lot. Usually I only play serious strategy games such as Civilization and my past forays into console games have been far less than satisfactory. Thanks to the other reviewers here I decided to give this one a try and I'm very glad I did. At first I was wondering if it is just an interactive story. I'm not much for the story aspects of games and it took several scenes before actual game play comes up. Surprisingly, I held in there and after the first couple short missions I was hooked. The story itself is not overly original but also not so common as to be boring. The main characters are likeable enough and as things progressed I found myself interested in what was going on and anxious to find out what would happen next. So then, the Pros: The Graphics, great! I wasn't sure what to think of the watercolor/cartoon/anime mix at first but after seeing it in action I'm hooked. While most modern games seem to be going for the "real as life" look this game looks softer, less in your face. Also on the plus side of things is the ease of play. It was easy to learn how things work and to understand the goals and objectives set out. I got an Xbox controller to use with it, my first time ever using one, and I'm having a great time with it. Another plus, to me, is the music. I often turn the music or all sound off when playing games because I usually find it distracting or somehow undesirable. This one is different and interesting is that parts of the music, while certainly different, is reminiscent of songs I've heard, some old and some not so old. On the Cons side of things I'm coming up a little short. I would prefer to not have go through a configuration launcher every time and sometimes the story plays on emotions in ways I'd rather it didn't. Sometimes the story scenes are a bit long and I would get impatient for the next mission. And of course there's always those times such as when my best gunner totally misses the house sized tank 20 feet in from of him and gets me ranting and wanting an undo/redo/wtf button. But that's part of luck and chance and it wouldn't be a real game without. None of these things warrant losing even one star so my rating stands at 5 out of 5. All in all I think this is one of the most refined and polished games I've ever played. It's done. Totally complete and playable on initial download. No waiting weeks or months for patches and updates. No hours spent grinding through forums hoping to find a fix for some inane problem. This game works and works well. When the next episode or book in the story is released for the PC I will most certainly buy it too. 5 out of 5 stars for this one and kudos for the developers. Well Done!

title: Overpriced and Uninspired
text: I had really hoped for more from this game. Sadly it's more or less Civ 5 in new clothes with most of Civ 5's best features lost in the translation. Same as many others I've waited years for them to "finish" civ 5 and thought this would be a good culmination of their work. Wrong! This is more like starting over with a big step backwards. I regret giving them my 50 bucks for this, it should have been downloadable content for civ 5. At least then some of the polish they'd achieved would have been carried over. UPDATE: Minus another star, was 3 now 2. I've played several games of this new civ so far, they go much faster than usual. There are some neat things and now that I've got used to the interface it's ok too. What isn't ok is having to play on only random maps. No scenarios, no meticulously setting up the perfect game. And I'm sorry to say, random gets boring and repetitive very fast. Hopefully soon they will release a map and scenario editor and given things like that have, for a very long time, been a part of Sid Meier's Civilization, it's pretty lame they release this game without it. IMHO. 2nd UPDATE: It's been a month now and still no update so there goes another star. On a positive note, the game does play nicely. It moves along with an ease I've not before noticed in any civ and the soft sounds for events don't make me cringe.

title: Great Keyboard - Great Price
text: First off I want to note that I got this when it was priced at $29.99, perhaps the best deal I've ever got on a keyboard. I replaced a CM Storm Trigger with this after the Storm developed connection issues after only 3 months, probably the worst deal I've ever got on a keyboard. I wish I had bought this one first because I like it better than the cm storm. It's much lighter and much, much easier to program. Obviously it doesn't have the nice cherry switches like the storm does and I am concerned on how long it will last, but it's a great keyboard and the touch is fine, I can't complain. At first I was worried about the green lighting, I thought it would look strange and be hard to see. To my surprise it looks great and is very easy to see. To my eyes I'd have to say it's easier to see than either red or blue light, both of which I've had before. And because I do all my typing with the keyboard resting between my indian style crossed legs it's light weight is great, so much better than having 3 pounds of keyboard digging into my legs. The only CON I've found is sometimes when I type the keys will squeak a little and that is a bit annoying. If it ever gets bad I'll just pull the caps and touch the springs up with a bit of oil. My only regret is that I didn't buy 2 or 3 of them when they were priced so low.

title: Fantastic, mostly
text: I received this mouse just a few hours ago and I love it. It did take me a little while to fully understand the programming software in order to make it do what I want. Now that I understand it, I don't have a single complaint. The Windows 7 x64 drivers installed without a glitch as did the programming software. I like that I was able to change the palm rest to make it higher than normal and I was able to adjust the side buttons forward to put them in just the right place. In the 4 hours I've been using it, it has used 17% of the charge in one battery, not too bad in my opinion. I look forward to using more as so far I am very pleased. UPDATE: It's 3 days later and I am in the process of returning it. I like it, a lot. I like how it feels and moves and nearly everything about it, except; Whenever I swap batteries when I plug the one to be charged into the receiver it disconnects from windows so I have to crawl under the desk and unplug/re-plug the usb cable. Mad Catz support told me they think it is a defective receiver but will not send a replacement unless I first send them this one. Thankfully Amazon is replacing it free of charge. UPDATE 2: A month later, problems are solved and I am loving this mouse. As others have mentioned, battery life could be better but so far it's fine with me. Going back up to 5 stars.

title: Thumbsticks are bad
text: The packaging certainly looked like a genuine Sony product, but this controller is terrible. L3 and R3 get stuck 100% of the time after being pressed, and my character just keeps lurching to the left until I pull them back up. For comparison, I have been using my original DualShocks for the entire lifetime of the PS4, and only just now started having problems with one thumbstick on one, and the battery life on the other. I don't know what they did other than putting a stupid light under the touchpad, but they ruined both thumbsticks on this version out of the box. The battery life is good, I guess.

title: Lights are a PITA.
text: I bought the K55 from corsair because my wife was tired of hearing the constant click click click fromy my razar keyboard. I wasn't wanting to drop a load of dough and needed an led backlit keyboard. This K55 looked liked the perfect fit for my needs. They key's are quite and responsive. That much I'm happy with. What I'm not quite so satisfied with is controlling the colors and lighting effects. The iCue software is anything but intuitive. Plus the FN+(number) to change the lighting doesn't work at all once booted into windows. I thought for awhile I had figured it out but the first time I launched a game the leds turned off. Okay that was interesting. I tried 3 other games. Each they'd load, lights off. Exit to the desktop the lights would come back on. Well guess what. I need to see my keyboard when gaming. Nothing in the documentation or support forums I've found has said anything about this. Anyway this is my first purchase of a Corsair product and based on this alone they won't be my first choice in the future.

title: Huge disappointment.
text: This is not a game for first timers, if i was a first timer who never played a final fantasy game before and this was my first it would destroy my whole image of the series. Incredibly stupid battle system, the story was wrapped up quick like someone made it up in the 10 minutes before their lunch break, vague characters which the story never mentions their past or why did they come to be with you, boring repetitive fetch or kill side quests and not even 5 minutes into the game and they throw the sex appeal at you with "Cindy" which i think her entire existence in the game is nothing but a forced sexual theme in a poor attempt to balance the all male cast. Not even the music was up to par. The story was 90% ffx with the whole idea of the main character dying after the final summon with a forced in death or two to make it emotional. Sorry, just didn't do it for me, by far the worst final fantasy game in the series. The kingsglaive movie was okay, basically the only good thing about this whole ff15 thing although I caught a hint of witcher from it... slowly losing your creativity squeenix.

title: This game had an impact on my life
text: I love this game I cannot express enough how much i adore this game, it is my absolute favorite i must have played it more than 12 times at least and some of my playtimes exceeded the 300 hours, and every time i play is like the first time very enjoyable touching sentimental and beautiful, wonderful story, amazing characters, awesome graphics, unbelievably beautiful soundtrack... There's just nothing wrong with this game it's perfection after that squaresoft went on a steady slope. I own each and every release of this game, ps2, ps3, vita and i just had to add the ps4 version to my collection and i am going to be playing more and more because i can never have enough of this beautiful spectacular game.

title: Awesome! See video
text: [[VIDEOID:c9bc14990518c1a54b1c7804e3d78a77]] Okay so this thing isn’t “heavy” but it definitely has a bit of weight that makes you trust it. And you should trust it too after watching that video haha. The plastic on the pieces is a really snug fit so you can tell it won’t fall apart on you, and the rotation of the lights on the bottom is pretty smooth. Wireless charging works on mine (if it didn’t idc, this thing is awesome). Haven’t tried the usb yet. Definitely worth the mere $16 I spent on this. Headphones are Senn HD6XX & Senn HD 280 Pro. Fully metal headphones I might get something more sturdy but for these, it’s perfect

title: PS4 Charging-Cooling base stand
text: works for dual controller charging as well as cools additionally -while the ps4 is stood securely vertical - vie dual 9mm fans in base that force air through the unit side vents & lets you feel the next-gen graphically intense games generated heat being pumped out the device effectively . Heat kills HW; this base actually lowers temps of entire PS4 between 15 degrees - to- 20 ° F (used thermal scan ) on my PS4 . Sturdy enough for two kids and cheap enough insurance . Additional USB ports and a button to disable the fans when you don't need them on ...not cheap looking , either . A Worthy PS4 accessory , for sure !

title: Pretty good
text: The game arrived very quickly and in good condition. However, though the gameplay is decent, there is much to be desired. AI pathing and attack priority is pretty messed up. Units will target workers before attacking units and defensive structures and, once engaged, they will pursue their targets until you tell them to do something else. Some of the larger units (titans, colossi, etc.) are so large and slow they need to be manually controlled at all times or else they will stand behind the front lines and walk back and forth like idiots until an opening to attack appears (combine this with the retarded priority and you get units that will walk back and forth behind the front lines trying to get at a unit on the other side even though there are enemies right next to him posing an immediate threat). Units need to deal more damage, as battles drag out much longer than they should.

title: sloppy console port
text: Wow what a disappointment. This was obviously a port that was rushed out just to make sales for the holiday season...product quality be damned. I can't believe Rockstar would make such a fine game on the Xbox/PS3 and then make such a horrible port. What can I say? Had problems installing it. Once installed, had problems getting it to play. Tried another computer, it installed, but then was forced to sign up for MS Live (even though it said only needed for multi-player). Runs like junk. Looks like junk. If you have an Xbox 360/PS3, buy it for that system. Definitely don't buy this as a gift for anyone unless you hate them!

title: It works. Comes down to preference. I'm good w/ floor fan, sweatband & puppy pad strips
text: Well, now that I have tried it, I can say that I really just prefer my usual simple silicone cover, a good sweat band, and the inclusion of a cut up puppy pad/incontinence pad placed between forehead and sweatband (sweatband holds it in place). Be sure it doesnt have attractants, and you'll find it a game changer for mopping up sweat and reducing/eliminating fog. The other thing I do is have a fan running near by. Never had any fog. I tried this because a lot of people seem to like the built in fan when playing hot sweaty fitness games like Supernatural. That is what I play, actually it is all I play. So being comfortable is important, and my DIY system seems to work fine. But I was curious, and while it works, it comes down to preference. Just so you know, this fan style is more for air movement around the unit, not a direct blast to face. I think that is what some people may think a fan of this style is. It is more for keeping moisture/fog from building on lens, and it totally works. Maybe I will have better idea once we get into some super hot humid weather. Maybe it will make a greater difference then. I will report back on that. Easy enough to hook up. Does not impede head strap use Does not interfere with charging docks (like anker)

title: doubles Oculus play time, comfortable fit, hugs back of head for relaxing app experience
text: It doubles play time without need for a physical battery pack. Nice option for those that use some apps laying down- there is no battery bracket to get in the way. The Oculus has about 2 hours of run time, or less. I use mine primarily for the workout/fitness app, "Supernatural-workout near, go far". At full charge, I will go 1.5 hours, with maybe 20 minutes left. Totally fine, so long as my Oculus is fully charged. If I want to do anything else, then I need to charge it. Or if anyone else wants to play. I have been meaning to buy a battery pack for my [[ASIN:B094Z85PXS X-super Home Adjustable Elite Strap with Battery Bracket]] but haven't done so yet, I have been just using it every single day as a regular strap. My husband bought me a battery pack but it is way too huge. So when this rechargeable strap came up as an option to try, I figured it was something worth checking out. The head strap is light and comfortable. The rear hugs the head, SO this is an excellent contender for those that play games, use apps that are conducive to relaxing, laying down. The fit relies entirely on the velcro straps (top & sides). I prefer the additional crank turn knob of my other strap, but this style is pretty popular and must have merit. The battery charges pretty quick. It holds about 2 hours of charge. I dont plan to have it as my daily strap, at least right now. I think I will keep it charged up, and have it on stand by for times I either failed to fully charge my Oculus, or when someone wants to use it after me and needs the extra juice. Or for after my evening workout session, and I want to go lay on the couch comfortably. Anyway, so far so good. If I experience anything else worth sharing, I will be back to do so.

title: Secure, durable. Totally plain looking but I think that's a good thing.
text: Plain, unassuming case. I LIKE that. It isn't fancy, it doesn't stand out. Anything could be inside. It fits my (well, my husbands Oculus Quest 2-- but I commandeered it for Supernatural) perfectly. Has plenty of room to store cord, extra face frames, the controllers, and my grips. The VR just nestles inside snug. Has added internal strap to secure the headset. And a mesh pocket for smaller accessories. Outer case is durable feeling, has a strap for use on luggage, a hand strap, and an optional long shoulder strap. Currently priced at $24.99. If they keep it at that price point, I would think this will garner more purchases over others I see. This is a perfectly good case, and if you like the clean, plain visual aspect of it, it is perfect (though I imagine the smooth surface could be dolled up with some stickers). The product description did an excellent job on describing this product and showing off what it looks like inside and out. The product is as expected. I dont need to stuff my Oculus in it as I pretty much use it at home every day a few times a day, but it is nice to have a secure spot for times when not in use, and of course for when I take it on the go.

title: nice coverage, good grips & straps, no interference with connection, haptic feedback
text: This is my first set of grips, and I am pleased to have them. I've been using them daily for about a week, a few times per day, for about an hour at a stretch. The attach easily enough and have not interfered with connectivity. I primarily use this while playing Supernatural, so if you play games that require a lot of batting at objects, then know that all is good with these grips. While I dont bash my hands into anything in my environment (big guardian space), I occasionally hit my Oculus Quest 2 as I swing my hands around at high speed. Also, with the colors, I can put the controllers on much quicker. Right is red, blue is left. Not only have wrist straps, but there is additional hand strap. So really, no fear of it flying out from hands accidentally. I already have a silicone cover, but this set including one is nice. Adds a pop of color. Everything was tucked into a small box, so I appreciate the smaller footprint. I dont know why I am hemming and hawing between a 4 & a 5. I think it is because I dont have experience with other grips to compare these to. But I am happy with them so far, and I have several hours of use on them.. so 5 it is. If I experience anything else, I will be back to update.

title: takes pressure off cheeks, easily adjusts in size, nose area reduces light gap, really good so far!
text: EDIT/UPDATE: This strap is still doing really well. Shortly after this review (Sep 2021), once I discovered Supernatural-Workout near, go far fitness app, I have been using it every single day for 60+ minutes at a time. I basically commandeered my husbands Oculus, and have been the only one using it. ZERO ISSUES. Now it is the end of December and I figured I would mention how well it has been holding up. This strap takes some pressure off my cheekbones. I could feel the difference right away. The head strap is a significant upgrade over the default strap. My husband and I are currently sharing the Oculus, and we're always having to adjust the strap. I think my head it bigger. Adjusting this strap is as easy as a turn of a dial. SO MUCH BETTER, easier, more comfortable. We both are really liking this so far. The silicon face cover is much better than the one that ships with the Oculus Quest 2. It is more robust, and I can feel the difference both when holding one in each hand, and once on the VR-- it is just more comfortable. ALSO, it has more material in the nose bridge area, which helps to fill up any gaps. There is a slit in the longer material which allows it to comfortably fit around various noses. Before I could see the floor and outside light, now it is pretty much all gone. This strap simply feels more secure over the default. Everything about it more comfortable and natural feeling. As for the battery pack holder, we currently do not have a battery pack to use so I cant comment on how well it holds one. But I can say that it is similar to a phone holder-- uses tension to hold it in place. I dont notice any added weight, or at least nothing that makes it uncomfortable by the addition of a more robust head strap and battery pack holder. The cut out of material that leads toward rear of the strap is not perfect. I dont see it impacting anything unless it peels off. Hopefully all remains good there. I am really quite pleased SO FAR. You better believe I will be back to update immediately if I experience anything bad, but I will also update if I experience/notice anything else worth sharing. I hemmed and hawed between a 4 and 5. 4 only because I havent had this long, but 5 because if it continues to be a good working item then it is something I would easily recommend for someone to try. The current price of <$40 (and now there is a coupon for a few bucks off), makes it competitively priced, and worth trying. Anyway, 5 it is!

title: A gaming headset that is not just for gaming.
text: I do not use an Xbox to play games although I do play some games. I do not use this headset for the games that I play. This headset is excellent for using with my PC and my Mac with excellent sound quality and a gaming headset feel and a futuristic look that is wireless. I can put my music on, put the headsets on and walk around and work without being wired to the computer. Which makes it fun to have a good quality stereo sound without being tide down. Who knows, one day I might even hook them up to my Xbox. OZ

title: Works out the box for Minecraft and Roblox, that's all I needed...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Very nifty controller pad accessory for your smartphone. * Built in thermoelectric/Peltier cooler. * Telescopic and will adjust to your smartphone length. * The cooler on the back is not fixed in the center, it is adjustable. This allows you to clear any camera humps your phone may have. * Buttons are mappable using the GameSir app, so you can play virtually any game. THE BAD: ------------ * Honestly, I don't know what's bad. I'm not a hardcore gamer. I just wanted something that will allow me to play roblox and minecraft out the box with my kids. I can never keep up with my kids on my smartphone because I hate playing games with touch controls. LOL! I've tried other brands like Flydigi, and I was completely lost in their mapping directions. This GameSir simply works out the box for Minecraft and Roblox. I didn't need to do any mapping. So that's 5-Stars from me!

title: Awesome cable! Got the job done for me...
text: I use a HDMI hub, which is also a universal remote. The cable that came with my PS5 has to go out from the PS5 and into this hub. This hub then goes out into my projector. I could never get 4k. However, if I connect the PS5 with it's original cable directly to the projector, then I could get 4k. So basically the cable I have connecting my hub to my projector is not getting the job done. I replaced it with this PowerA cable and voila! The PS5 is now delivering 4k even with the hub as the middle man. 5-Stars!

title: A superior horizontal stand to the PS5's version, but you should put the case holder on the left...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Love how this idea creates a nice gap at the bottom to truly create venting. * The brackets can be fitted on either side. Which is a good thing because if you follow the stock photos, they put it on the right which blocks existing vents. So I put my case holder on the left. * This method also makes moving and budging the PS5 easier, so long as your hands are supporting both brackets while you're moving it. The PS5's round stand always comes off when I budge the system. THE BAD: ------------ * Something I missed when I was looking at the product photos. You actually have to flip the console upside down. So the PS5 logo is facing the ground. This is a little concerning to me. This means you'll be inserting your discs upside down, meaning silver shiny side facing the ceiling when you insert a disc. Does this have any long-term effects on the hardware? I've done some research, and it seems there won't be any harm done to it. You should read for yourself. Just search google for "THE TRUTH ABOUT LAYING YOUR PS5 DOWN 'INCORRECTLY." It's an article by SVG. I give this idea and product 5-Stars!

title: Works with my X-Arcade stick out the box...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * 10k games!!! * It recognized my X-Arcade stick, so I was then able to configure other usb controllers. * Works for Pi3, and 3B+ * Basic, non-confusing skin. THE BAD: ------------ * As mentioned above, the skin is basic, which is good if you're a beginner, but might be bland if you're used to all sorts of arcade skins. * Learning curve is very small. You need for it to recognize at least one controller so you can start moving around and learn the settings. You know what? For $20, this is 5-Stars! Here's a tip, If the system doesn't recognize any of your controllers, plug in a keyboard and navigate by the arrows to get your game controllers configured.

title: Nice convenient dual docking station for your PS5 controllers...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Aesthetically matches the PS5 nicely. * Easy docking as advertised. * Fast charging as advertised as well. * Price. THE BAD: ------------ * Lightweight, cheap build. * The charging port is on the side. Which prevents you from hiding the entire cable. If it's in the back, you can just drop the cable behind the cabinet. So to hide the cable, I have the dock in a, I guess you would call it, lengthwise position instead of width. This way, the cable port is now in the back, but your controllers are no longer displaying horizontally. Look at my pictures, you'll see what I mean. I'll go 4-Stars.

title: Awesome headset with a brilliantly designed wireless usb-c dongle...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Razer brand... they make good stuff. * Aesthetically very nice. Color coordinates with the PS5 perfectly! * Build quality is terrific, and the sound it delivers is awesome. I'm not an audiophile, so if you're not either, you'll be more than impressed. * Mic is bendable allowing for great voice capture. * The foam cushions for your ears are very comfortable and snug. * For wireless connection, the usb-c dongle takes into account that the PS5 has USB-A ports to the right of the USB-C port, so they efficiently designed it so that it doesn't cover the USB-A ports. Brilliant! * The dongle connects to our phones and Nintendo switch with no issues either. * Packaging is very premium. The foam cut-outs that the headset sits in are high quality. You're not going to want to throw away the box. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing at all. We love this headset! 5-Stars!

title: A very nice mouse with many bells and whistles, but build quality is questionable...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Very smooth working mouse. * 7 programmable buttons. * Bluetooth or usb dongle connection. * Two battery slots. You don't have to fill both slots, you can use either one AA, or one AAA battery. I've never seen this before. * The best mouse I've ever used in terms of adapting to different surfaces. You really don't need a mouse pad. * Mechanical switches. * Razer brand-name and dependability. THE BAD: ------------ * This is a high end mouse that feels like a cheap $10 mouse. It weighs virtually nothing. With a AA battery installed, it's 3.5 ounces. Keep in mind, I'm not a gamer. Is this what all gamer mouses feel like? They need it lightweight for some sort of advantage? I don't know. My cheaper $30 Logitech mouse has more heft than this mouse. So if you don't like lightweight plastic stuff, then don't get this. I'll go 4-Stars.

title: Terrific design allowing you to charge four more joycons...
text: THE GOOD: ------------- * Truly awesome design. * Can charge 4 extra joycon controllers. * I tested with 3rd party joycons and it charged them too. * Slots for two switch cartridges. * USB out port. THE BAD: ----------- * I am not sure if mine is defective. The black side never turns red when charging like the red side, it's always green. You might say it's because the joycon is already fully charged. But when I remove the same joycon, and put it to the red side, the led lights turn red to indicating charging. But for what it's worth, when it's on the black side, even though the led doesn't turn red, the lights on the joycon itself is blinking as if it's charging. So until the seller can answer these questions, I'll rate this 3-Stars.

title: Very nice steering wheel if you're not a hardcore nitpicky gamer...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Wheel has good heft. The unit is a little over 7 lbs. * Wheel cover is made of genuine leather. * Buttons are nice placed and in close reach. * Wheel has a table clamp. * Pedal unit is also high quality at over 7 lbs as well, no flex. * Trueforce feature with strong feedback. This feature helps with increasing immersion. * Compatible with PC as well as Xbox THE BAD: ----------- * Braking can be difficult, seems like there is more resistance the more you brake. * Price point is not competitive with previous models. The improvements are slight, so unless you can get this on sale, I would look at their older models and pay below $300. * Although Trueforce feature is a positive above, in reality, there are not many games currently that are compatible with the Trueforce feature. * The pedal unit made me bleed. LOL! When you pull the pedal unit out of the box, naturally your hand will want to support it by holding it from the bottom of the base. Something pricked me, and my finger started to bleed. I flipped it over to see what could cut me, and I realize their is a rectangular mold with really sharp corners. Look at my pictures to what I'm talking about, so you can avoid getting hurt yourself. Honestly, I'm quite annoyed that I bled while reviewing this thing. You don't expect to get hurt by game accessories. Because it's such a naturally tendency for your hands to support things at the bottom, I'm 100% sure others will get pricked by those corners as well. If Logitech is reading this, please provide a warning to your consumers. As for me, I will just round out the corners of that rectangle mold with a Dremel. Subtracting 1 star for the price point and value proposition compared to pervious models, and I'm subtracting another star for being the first game accessory ever to make me bleed. LOL! 3-Stars.

title: Too complicated for the layman...
text: THE GOOD: ------------- * Terrific build quality. Good heft * USB-C THE BAD: ----------- * Not for layman. Manual is useless. You are basically on your own from the get go, and you just figure out things blindly. I figured the FLYDIGI app is what I needed, and sure enough I found it on the Playstore. The app uses lingo and terms only gamers probably understand. Classic mode, native mode, mapping mode, Flashplay mode, etc. There is a big learning curve to understand what all these modes mean and does. Next to word CONNECTED, is the word UNACTIVATED. Apparently you need to activate something, and it gives you a choice of using U-Tool or the PC. What is U-Tool? I don't know, but the app assumes you do know. So I googled "U-TOOL flydigi" and I discover it's some sort of rooting dongle. So then I figure, I'll check out the PC method. For this option, they tell you to go to their website and download the PC tool. Except, the only option is an Android APK. SMH. They have an email, and they seem to have a community, but I'm not that much into gaming to put in this type of effort. I wanted a controller that would hold my phone, so I can play roblox with my kids, that's it. LOL! Because I hate the touch controls in Roblox. This is too complicated. I'll go 3-Stars! I'm sure this is 5-Stars to people into gaming. Knocking 2 stars for the lack of directions.

title: Awesome dock that color coordinates with the Nintendo theme...
text: Gets the job done! No more having to remove my protective case! However, understand that the power adapter is not included. I happen to have gotten another accessory set that includes everything, but the dock wouldn't seat my switch with a case on. I needed to remove my case every time. That is the reason I got this dock. Your Switch won't be sitting up neatly, but it is much more convenient to just plug and play, instead of having to remove the case. What's also great is that it color coordinates with everything in the other set. This is the other set I'm talking about: https://www.amazon.com/review/R2SU9HR7308F1Y/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm? ie=UTF8&ASIN=B08KVPT7DN With the kit in the above link, you'll get a case, HDMI cable, power adapter for your Switch, and a dock. If your Switch doesn't have a protective case, then you might want to consider that link. But I got this dock as well because I do use a case, and it was a hassle to remove it every time. This dock is 5-Stars all the way!

title: You no longer have to remove your Switch case to dock...
text: If you have a case on your Nintendo switch, docking can be a hassle, especially with 3rd party docks, you will need to remove your case every time. I decided having the switch docked upright neatly is no longer a priority. Now, I just plug in the usb-c and let the switch lay on the table. Much quicker than having to remove the case, and you're not missing out on anything other than your Switch not sitting upright. A minor issue is that this dock needs to be plugged directly into a wall. There is only three ports: 1 for the HDMI, 1 for USB-C to your Switch, 1 spare USB port to charge an accessory. So technically, you never have to see the dock, as long as you plan ahead and have long enough cables. But I would like to switch cables easily, so I'm using an extension cord to bring the dock to the table. 5-Stars!

title: Best keyboard I have ever owned, never going back to normal keyboards...
text: I tried gaming keyboards before, and was never impressed. But I believe my mistake was that the keyboards were not mechanical. I believe they can be gaming, but not mechanical. You need the ones that are mechanical! I don't think I'll ever go back to ordinary or membrane keyboards. The spring and tactile feel of this keyboard is awesome! I tend to be a nostalgic person anyway, so I love the retro feel of these keyboards. You also no longer need to worry about batteries since it's required to be plugged in via USB. The lights are cool, and the build quality is excellent. It is not light and cheap, this little guy weighs in at 34.4 ounces. No weak buttons, or touch buttons. The volume scroller is amazing!!! It is cold to the touch because it is made of metal, and feels oddly satisfying when scrolling. Everything is tactile, every key is springy. This was how things were made in the past. 5-Stars all the way!

title: The best part of this case is the one piece design of the joycon covers...
text: This is kind of a unique case. I wanted something dockable to avoid taking the case on and off. However, keep this in mind, "dockable" only applies to the original Switch dock. It will not dock on third party docks that are designed differently, I've tried since I have several in my collection. But the most unique thing about this case is the covers for the joycons. The shell that covers the back of the main body is made of the usual hard plastic, however, the cases for the joycon are a one piece flexible rubber, which is a pleasant surprise. Normally, the cases for the joycon would also be hard plastic and would come in two pieces that would sandwich the joycon. This one piece design is so much more convenient! 5-Stars all the way!

title: Great looking, solid accessory for the Nintendo Switch...
text: Beautiful Nintendo Switch accessory. I'm just a daddy who plays occasionally, and get most of these accessories for my kids who are not yet 10 yrs old. What I'm saying is that we are not hardcore gamers, and don't get into the technical aspects of these controllers. Some gamers can tell the difference when something is a split second off. LOL! If you're a casual gamer, believe me you'll love these. The work and feel just as good as the original joycons, but you get better grip for your Splatoon 2 battles. LOL! That's what I use it for most. 5-Stars!

title: Great set, but the dock will not fit your Switch if you use a tempered glass screen protector...
text: This is a beautiful colorful set! The case is obviously designed to look like Mario's outfit. You're getting a nice Nintendo theme without the Nintendo price tag. LOL! It comes with a dock, the power adapter, HDMI cable and a USB-C cable. It even has a strap to carry the case via shoulders if you wish. A great on the go solution. Unfortunately, I'm going to knock off 1 star. This would be 5 stars, but I'm rating it a 4. The reason is because the dock is useless to anybody who puts a tempered glass on their switch. The fitting is so perfect for the Switch, there is no room for anything else. I can't even force it in. I can see the plug on the dock pushing up the edge of my screen protector. If I force it, I'm sure it will crack the screen protector and scratch the real screen underneath. Everybody nowadays love to put cases and screen protectors on their gadgets. That is why marketplaces are inundated with smartphone accessories, as well game console and computer accessories. Why would you not take this into consideration in your design? The dock is a big part of the price tag, and it'll be unfortunate for those who can't use it. I'll only knock 1 star since it should work for people who do not use tempered glass on their Switches, and it might even work for those who only use a thin film protector. But hardened glass protectors are very popular, and I feel this should have been taken into account.

title: Super fun open world adventure MMO game...
text: This is a pretty nice MMO (massive multiplayer online) game. In this game, you will play, Fenyx, a demi-god. If you enjoy Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, you will like this game, but it has enough originality of its own. Soundtrack during the game is great, and the story line is open-ended, so there is potential for sequels. The best part of this game is the open world adventures. The entire map is open from the outset, unlike other games where you made need to unlock section by section. If you enjoy flying in games, you can do that once you get wings! The game is very fun, colorful and vibrant. Ultimately, you want to defeat Typhon. We like this game so much, we started wondering what it would look like on the more powerful consoles, and boy, it does look so much better on the ps5. But, this game is for the Switch, and we know, graphically, it's unfair to compare to the ps5. This game is 5-Stars!

title: Cannot dock with a case, not even a thin one...
text: I'm still in search of a dock that can accommodate a switch with a case. A previous one I had was too narrow width-wise, so it couldn't seat. The design on this one seems pretty open, look at the pictures, you'll see the width is wide. So I had hopes this could be the one! My switch with the thin case sat on the dock with no issues at all. That's what I was hoping for based on the design. But I realized of a new issue. Even if you can seat your Switch with a case, it might not charge. The reason is because your case creates a rise that prevents the usb-c port and plug to fully connect. Logically, I knew about this already. But I anticipated that the contact would be enough for it to charge. Sadly, the answer is no. It needs to be 100% docked. The only solution is to modify the case, like cutting out a slot to allow it to fully seat with no rise. This isn't something I'm going to subtract a star for. The dock does it's job perfectly fine when I take my switch out of the case. But just a FYI to those who are trying to do what I'm doing. This is still a 5-Stars product!

title: Nice looking fighting stick with Sanwa compatible internals...
text: Nice fighting stick for Super Smash Bros! I know the hardcore gamers can pick apart this stick, but my kid is 8 yrs old and is blown away by this, and that's all that matters. He gets dibs on this stick whenever we play Super Smash. For the serious gamers out there. The good news is that all the parts seem to be Sanwa compatible from the joystick to the buttons. So if you want to, you can replace the components. An 8 yr old doesn't know how to complain about a missed combo. LOL! So, I won't be doing any modification. This stick is fine as is. The red top of this stick is not permanent, it is a decorative plate, and can be replaced with other plates. They do include an extra design for you, but we happen to love red, so we won't be changing anything. Another thing to note is that when you plug in the USB-C cable, it is simply for power for wired play. It doesn't do any charging because there is no internal rechargeable battery. If you want to play wireless, you need to use two AA batteries, which they claim can give you 30 hrs of gameplay. We'll see about that. This is a 5-Star product!

title: Too light, no SL/SR top cover...
text: Of all the 3rd party joycons I've tried, this is probably my least favorite. What caught my eye was the charging cable. I thought it was pretty unique and unlike others. However, I don't think you can use it to charge other joycons. It was made specifically for theirs. I connected to another brand of joycons and there doesn't seem to be any reaction. I will update this review if I discover anything new on this front. So there are two main things why this has been my least favorite: 1. Weight... At 1.7 oz. each, this is the lightest third party joycon I have. It is cheap! The original is 2.5 oz. each. 2. No SL/SR top covers. So if you split these up to play multiplayer games, your SL/SR buttons will be hard to press. I'll rate this 3 stars. For 3rd party, I prefer this set a review a while ago. It is 2 oz. each and they include the SL/SR top covers. https://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-reviews/R3UHC1PVPNANJ3/ref=cm_cr_othr_d_rvw_ttl?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B08HQX1HKM

title: Officially licensed Nintendo Switch retro controller with insane battery life...
text: The design of this controller is classic/retro. It reminds you of the Super NES days. Here are some things to note: -Weighs 4.3 ounces -40 hrs battery life -Motion Control supported -PDP is officially licensed to make Nintendo products -USB-C is included, but it is short. So you probably won't be using it when charging. -NO NFC -ZL and ZR buttons are curved in a way that will allow your index fingers to rest on. Depending on how you feel about the placement of the d-pads and buttons, this controller may or may not be worth the money to you. If you're not completely happy about the layout, then check out the 8bitdo SN30 controller. Overall, that seems to be a better controller, but it all depends on what you value more. If 40 hrs of battery life is more important to you, then get the PDP. In any case, the 8bitdo is a good alternative if you're not sold on this PDP. https://www.amazon.com/8Bitdo-SN30-Controller-Windows-macOS-Android/dp/B0748S1VDC/ref=sr_1_4?dchild=1&keywords=8bitdo+sn30+pro&qid=1604087284&sr=8-4 This would be a 4 star controller, if not for the battery life, since it's price in the same ballpark as the 8bitdo SN30. But the fact that PDF is officially licensed and it has the battery advantage, then it brings it back to 5-Stars! You need to decide what's more important to you when deciding between these two controllers.

title: Honestly, the perfect switch lite case, please read why...
text: You probably don't think of FULL vs HALF BODY when searching for cases, do you? Initially, we got one of those soft TPU ones, but then we realized the top is exposed. If you want FULL body protection, these 2 piece hard shell cases are what you want. However, the issue with these full body cases is that most of them create the mold around the X,Y,A,B buttons. This makes the buttons feel almost flush to the surface, so you don't have a good tactile feel for the buttons. The good news about this full body case is that it DOES NOT mold around the buttons. It is completely cut-out, so you get 100% feel for the buttons. This is an awesome case that checks all the boxes for us: 1. Is it full body? Check! 2. Do you have a good feel for the X,Y,A,B buttons? Check! 3. Is it cute and daughter approved? Check! The cute matching joystick caps are just icing on the cake. This is 5-Stars all the way!

title: Upper and lower coverage, Joy-cons detachable, & unit can be docked!
text: This is a hard plastic case that comes with upper and lower molds to protect your entire switch. The joy cons have their own upper and lower molds too, so they are still detachable with the case on. Lastly, it is dockable! I like these types of cases better than the soft TPU types because usually those are just 1 rubber mold that keeps the top exposed and your joy cons are not detachable unless you remove the system from the case. You have no such concerns with this case. We love it! Look at the pictures and look at the fine scratches on the case. Those scratches would be on the Switch if not for the case. Get yourself one! 5-Stars!

title: This set will take up 2 usb ports...
text: I've been using wireless keyboards and mouses for a decade, so my mind had certain expectations. I once read about a wired set where the mouse is connected to the keyboard, and then 1 wire connects to the computer. This was like 5 yrs ago. It's now 2020, and based on something I read 5 yrs ago, I assumed it is industry standard now. LOL! But I was wrong, this takes up 2 ports just like the 1980's, just like the 1990's, just like the 2000's. The keyboard itself is fine. Feels a little on the cheap side due to how light it is. I'm not sure I'm willing to put up with all these wires. But this was not the products fault, it was the user's fault for making assumptions. As a matter fact, I can't find any gaming sets on Amazon that uses 1 wire described in the article I read years ago. SMH.

title: Half vs Full Body cover... this is full body.
text: This is probably something you don't think about, we certainly didn't... We just searched for Nintendo Switch Lite cases and picked one out. Initially, we got one of those soft TPU ones, but then we realized the top is exposed. So we continued searching and we found this listing. If you want FULL body protection, these 2 piece hard shell cases are what you want. However, you should consider this "con" before making your decision... You see the Switch buttons and directional pad protrude above the surface only by a little, so by placing a case layer on top, it makes the buttons almost feel flush to the surface. It's not completely flush, they are still raised above the case, but barely. You will need to feel for yourself and decide if this is right for you. I still give the case 5 stars because it does the job, and includes 2 glass screen protectors and cute thumb grips. A lot of bang for your buck!

title: You become a worse player!
text: So we gave our Wii new life in this "Stay at Home" world. I bought the Wii when it first came out, back when I had no children. LOL! I have two kids now and the Wii is getting a new life. But I digress... about these guns. Three things I don't like.... 1. You're kinda inserting your wiimote in at an angle. You basically place your wiimote on top of the gun mold "bed," but it cannot clear yet until you angle it and start to insert it into the connector. Then you can push it down flat. Connecting plugs and ports at an angle is uncomfortable to me. I feel eventually you will ruin the connector or port. 2. So in most Wii shooting games, the B button is your trigger, it is the button on the back of the Wiimote. So all these gun accessories are built so that when you pull the trigger, the mechanism inside then clicks the B button. So for a good gun accessory, the trigger on the gun mold should be as easy and as quick as clicking the B button on the Wiimote. Well, that's not the case with this gun, so you become a worse player. There is more resistance with the trigger, as well as more travel time. Travel time is how long it takes for you to completely pull the trigger. When you're just playing around with it and pulling the trigger. It's just like any other toy gun, you don't think anything about it. But when you start to play wii games, you will see that you got wore. Because all that extra time adds up. 3. I wanted my kids to be able to use it, but the handle plus trigger width was just too wide for a 5 yr old's hands. She ended up using two hands and spent more time focusing on pressing the trigger than aiming. So this is not good for little kids with small hands. For little kids with small hands, I recommend something called the "Wii blasters." This was a set that came out around 2011. It comes with 2 guns and a game code for BIG TOWN SHOOT OUT. The game codes have since expired, but people are still selling these guns.

title: This is the one to get!
text: I got both this version as well as the generic wii2hdmi that most are selling, and I've found out that not all wii to hdmi adapters are created equally. With the generic one, I see more wavy diagonal lines. With the MayFlash, the picture is smoother, the diagonal lines are gone. You need to go to your wii setting and set it to wide screen and 480p. You also need to go to your display source and set it to widescreen as well. Everything looks proportional, the image is not stretched. This is a keeper, the other one is being returned. BTW, I should mention that I'm using an ultra short throw projector with a 120" screen. With such a big image, maybe it is easier for me to see imperfections. So that should tell you how good this adapter is. It got rid of the lines I was seeing with the generic version. So on smaller screens, surely this adapter will do a great job for you.

title: Nintendo Switch brought me here....
text: My PS3 controllers are now getting a second life due to the Nintendo Switch. But I never knew it was such a hassle to get the PS3 controllers to charge without the actual PS3 system. Smartphone wall adapters DO NOT work. Third party docking products on Amazon do not come with a power adapter, only USB cables. Which means they probably require you to have your PS3 on. I've asked if Smartphone wall adapters will work with those third party docks, they say yes, but I don't trust the answer. I kept searching and ran onto this official Playstation product. This is just what the doctor ordered! Actually, a computer will charge your ps3 controllers too, but I'd like all my game accessories in my media cabinet. This adapter tucks in the back of my cabinet and the ps3 controllers are now charging inside my cabinet out of sight, out of mind. $10 and it's an official item. Doesn't get any better!

title: Wavebird owners, this is the adapter to buy!
text: July 15, 2020 UPDATE: -------------------------- This is not necessarily a review update, but more of a FYI, or food for thought. Though this is an excellent item, I've since discovered other products on the market that does the same job at a fraction of a price. There are adapters, for less than $10, that plug into your Switch, and it has 4 gamecube ports. I realized that for my use case scenario, I over spent. The main benefit of these Retro Fighter adapters is if you're using WIRED gamecube controllers. This way, you don't have wires running to and from your switch. You can just place the adapter at your feet, and the wires will be running from your feet to your hands. But it's overkill if you're using Wave Bird receivers. You are going wireless on top of wireless. There wasn't any lag issues, everything was fine. But you're paying a premium to do that. With those 4 port adapters. You plug it into your switch, and you can sill be wireless if you're using Wave Bird receivers. The downside is simply aesthetics because your switch will have these adapters plugged into it. But man, you can use 4 wave bird receivers for around $10 versus having to spend about $68 ($17 x 4) to use the retro fighter adapter, since each adapter is only good for one controller. Food for thought! ORIGINAL REVIEW: ---------------------- Much better than the 8bitdo design. Not sure why 8bitdo insisted on their design, but because they did, they lose out on customers who own wavebird controllers. Their Gbros is only good for wired gamecube controlers. You could try and hack off some of the plastic to accommodate the wavebird receiver. But why pay more to do more modding? The Warrior adapter is less expensive and doesn't need modifications. Easy to pair too. Just hold the HOME and O button until it blinks, then go to your Switch, and go to Change Grip/Controller, once you're there it will automatically discover the adapter and a controller icon will appear. Now, plug in your wavebird receiver and turn on your gamecube controller. Awesome!
